title: Removing Masks
summary: Clear step-mask overrides without changing channel mask defaults.
prose:
On the Masks page, hold a step and press K2 to clear its step-mask overrides. With no grid keys held, hold K1 and press K2 to clear all step-mask overrides on the selected channel. Both actions preserve channel mask defaults, which apply wherever an explicit step override is absent. Held steps take precedence even while K1 is down. Other channels are unaffected.

[Removing masks demo](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=J1ckUZvhFJ0&t=1823s)

title: Merge Modes
summary: Set how assigned patterns supply trigs, notes, velocities and note lengths to a channel.
prose:
Use one shared Strategy selector for channel output. Press grid (14,8) to cycle Skip → Only → All → Foundation → Fragments, wrapping after Fragments. On Merge modes, select Strategy with E2 and turn E3 through the same choices; E3 stops at the first and last choice. A successful choice requests immediately, without K3 Apply.

Strategy is the requested choice. Active is what is sounding; Pending is an accepted change waiting for its boundary, or NONE. While stopped, a valid choice applies immediately. During playback, Boundary names NEXT CYCLE or NEXT PATTERN.

Foundation controls trigs only. Note, velocity and length merge settings remain active. Fragments controls all four attributes. Retained note, velocity and length settings are labelled inactive and their values read as the saved mode followed by SAVED, for example AVERAGE SAVED. Those rows and their grid buttons do not edit saved values while Fragments is active. Select Skip, Only or All to restore the retained settings.

Foundation needs a valid assigned anchor. A refused request leaves the cursor at FOUNDATION and shows NEEDS ANCHOR, while Active and Pending keep their accepted values. The next forward detent or grid press reaches Fragments.

[Merge modes demo](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=J1ckUZvhFJ0&t=2065s)

details.title: Accepted state and refusal
details.text: Active and Pending identify accepted output, separately from the requested Strategy cursor. Foundation without a valid assigned anchor shows NEEDS ANCHOR and does not apply; the cursor remains at Foundation so the next forward choice reaches Fragments.

details.title: Attribute ownership
details.text: Foundation owns trigs only. Fragments owns trigs, notes, velocity and length. Its retained note, velocity and length settings are inactive and read, for example, AVERAGE SAVED; selecting Skip, Only or All restores them. The saved trig merge (Skip, Only or All) is kept while Foundation is Active and is restored from the Strategy selector.

title: Trig Merge Modes
summary: Select All, Skip or Only to determine which overlapping pattern trigs play.
prose:
Skip, Only and All are the first three choices of the shared Strategy selector. They define how trigs are combined across assigned patterns:

* **All**: Trigs will apply if they appear on a step in any selected pattern.
* **Skip**: Trigs will apply only if they appear on a step in exactly one selected pattern. If a trig appears on a step in multiple patterns, it won't activate.
* **Only**: Trigs will apply only if they appear on a step in more than one selected pattern, ignoring those that appear in just one.

title: Note Merge Modes
summary: Select Average, Higher, Lower or a priority pattern for merged note values.
prose:
These modes determine how note values are handled when steps overlap:

* **Average**: Average the contributing note values and round to the nearest integer, choosing the greater integer at an exact half (1.5 becomes 2; -1.5 becomes -1; -0.5 becomes 0). One contributor passes through unchanged. The result then uses the configured scale and pentatonic processing.
* **Higher**: Add the difference between the highest and lowest contributing note values to their rounded average. One contributor passes through unchanged; the result then uses the configured scale and pentatonic processing.
* **Lower**: Subtract the rounded average from twice the lowest contributing note value: `2 * lowest - rounded_average`. One contributor passes through unchanged; the result then uses the configured scale and pentatonic processing.
* **Pattern**: To prioritise a specific pattern's note values during conflicts, hold the note merge button and select the desired pattern. You can even select patterns that aren't current asigned to the active channel.

By default, notes will snap to the pentatonic version of the currently active scale to assist with avoiding unpleasant harmonic interactions. This can be disabled in _Mosaic_'s settings.

details.title: Reading the results
details.text: Two patterns with notes 60 and 64 average to 62. Higher adds the difference between them (4) to the mean (62) to give 66; Lower gives 2 x 60 - 62 = 58. With the pentatonic snap on, these results are then moved onto the pentatonic scale, so switch it off in the Mosaic params when you want to hear the plain merge results. Tap grid (15,8) to cycle Average, Higher and Lower.

details.title: Independent listening extension
details.text: The four-step visual comparison plays Average 62, 65, 69, 65 and Higher 65, 69, 72, 76. The recorded merge comparison uses different source patterns: its Average phrase is 62, 69, 64, 64. Try it as a separate extension after completing the visual comparison, rather than using it to check these exact notes.

recipes.title: Build the recording: Average, then Higher

title: Velocity Merge Modes
summary: Select Average, Higher, Lower or a priority pattern for merged velocity values.
prose:
These settings affect how velocity values are calculated for overlapping steps:

* **Average**: Average the contributing velocities and round to the nearest integer, choosing the greater integer at an exact half. One contributor passes through unchanged.
* **Higher**: Add the difference between the highest and lowest contributing velocities to their rounded average.
* **Lower**: Subtract the rounded average from twice the lowest contributing velocity: `2 * lowest - rounded_average`.
* **Pattern**: To use a specific pattern's velocity values, hold the velocity merge button and press the pattern's select button.

details.title: Reading the results
details.text: Higher and Lower are calculated from the mean and the range of the contributing velocities, so Higher can be above the highest source and is limited to 127. Tap grid (16,8) without K1 to cycle Average, Higher and Lower; the cycle wraps back to Average.

title: Length Merge Modes
summary: Select Average, Longer, Shorter or a priority pattern for merged note durations.
prose:
These modes dictate how the duration of notes is calculated for overlapping steps:

* **Average**: Average the contributing lengths and round to the nearest integer, choosing the greater integer at an exact half. One contributor passes through unchanged. Source lengths account for interruption by the next trig in that pattern.
* **Longer**: Add the difference between the longest and shortest contributing lengths to their rounded average. One contributor passes through unchanged.
* **Shorter**: Subtract the rounded average from twice the shortest contributing length: `2 * shortest - rounded_average`. One contributor passes through unchanged. Only the mean is rounded at this stage, so fractional source lengths can still produce fractional Longer or Shorter results.
* **Pattern**: To apply a specific pattern's length values, hold the length merge button and press the pattern's select button.

Length merge modes are set by holding shift (K1) and pressing the velocity merge mode button. Numeric merging retains zero and negative length results. For ordinary note playback, including delayed strums, a nonpositive effective length sends Note On followed by Note Off in the same scheduler pulse, without advancing musical time. This describes MIDI event order, not the sound or response of a connected instrument.

details.title: Worked example: lengths 2 and 4
details.text: Two patterns play notes 2 steps and 4 steps long on the same steps. Average gives 3 steps (the mean). Longer gives 3 + (4 - 2) = 5 steps. Shorter gives 2 x 2 - 3 = 1 step. Longer is therefore not simply the longest source, and Shorter not simply the shortest. Hold K1 and tap grid (16,8) to cycle Average, Longer and Shorter; the cycle wraps back to Average.

details.title: Compare short and sustained notes
details.text: The numeric comparison starts with source lengths 2 and 4 channel steps. Average gives 3; Longer gives 5; Shorter gives 1. Keep pitch and velocity fixed and inspect the Note Off after each Note On: the interval between them is the played gate length. An ordinary nonpositive result releases in the same pulse. A receiving instrument’s envelope can change the audible tail, so use the MIDI gate to distinguish these settings.

title: Note Dashboard
summary: Open Output to inspect the selected channel’s last note or a held step’s resolved output.
prose:
Choose Output from Channel tasks to inspect the last note played by the selected channel. **Note** shows the note and its chord voices. **Vel / Len** shows velocity and length. **Step** identifies the source step. **Degree** shows the pattern degree and the merged result, for example +2 > +3 MERGED. **Pitch** shows the scale pitch and any Harmony change, for example E4 > G4 HARMONY. **Sent** shows the note sent, or the reason none was sent: MUTED or REST.

Hold a step to inspect that step’s output, including the stages of a [Harmony](#harmony) event.

details.title: Output follows the selected channel
details.text: Select a channel with its row-1 button and Output shows that channel. A channel that has not played a note since playback started reads NO EVENT in every row. Start playback to fill the rows with its last note; hold a step to see what that step plays.

title: Clocks, Swing and Shuffle
summary: Set independent channel rates and Swing or Shuffle. Channel X settings inherit global feel settings.
prose:
Set the global composition tempo in Song tasks → Tempo / feel. Every Song slot uses this tempo. Open Channel tasks → Clock to set a division or multiplication for each channel; differing clock rates let channels run at different speeds relative to the shared tempo.

Set channel Swing to move notes closer together or farther apart. Swing ranges from -50 to 50. Use it to vary off-grid timing, including jazz or funk rhythms. Shuffle uses more complex patterns based on 21echoes’ [Cyrene](https://github.com/21echoes/cyrene), with selectable feel and basis. Channels can use independent settings.

If a channel's swing/shuffle settings are not set ("X"), they will take the global setting, which is set on the Song page's Tempo and feel screen. Selecting "X" again after choosing a local Swing or Shuffle mode restores global mode inheritance, just like an untouched channel; choosing either mode explicitly overrides the global mode. While playback is running, confirmed changes on this channel page take effect at the next global song-pattern boundary, including a repeat of the same pattern. They do not take effect immediately or at the next step of a shorter channel loop. While stopped, confirmed changes apply immediately.

[Clocks, swings and shuffle demo](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=J1ckUZvhFJ0&t=2623s)

details.title: Vertical list controls
details.text: Open Channel tasks → Clock. The vertical list shows Rate and the channel’s feel settings. Turn E2 to select Rate, then E3 to choose its division or multiplication. Press K3 to apply or K2 to cancel. Selecting a local Swing or Shuffle mode changes which feel rows are available. To make a bass move at half the main step rate, select /2 and apply; the rhythm keeps its notes while its channel advances less often. Feel source is read-only and E2 skips it; its value identifies the source of the resolved feel settings.

details.title: Rate default
details.text: The default Rate /1 gives one channel step per sixteenth note. /2 halves the channel speed. Swing and Shuffle change only the timing between steps, not which notes play.

title: Memory (undo and redo)
summary: Undo or redo the selected channel’s mask and trig-lock edits, including recorded edits.
prose:
Memory retains all mask and trig-lock actions, including recorded actions. Use the norns encoder to navigate the selected channel’s history.

Open Channel Editor and choose History from Channel tasks. The Memory screen shows your position in the channel's memory, the selected action, and how many actions you can still undo and redo.

- Use E3 to step back through past actions or forward towards more recent ones.
- Press K3 to jump directly to the latest action.
- Press K2 to return to the beginning of the memory.

To jump to the latest action and erase all subsequent memory, hold shift (K1) and press K3. To jump to the first action and erase all memory recorded after it, hold K1 and press K2.

[Memory demo](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iGx5fmrbatA&t=202s)

details.title: Position, floor and branching
details.text: The counter shows the current position and the total, for example 2 of 2. 0 of 2 is the floor: the oldest state, before any retained edit. Turn E3 left to undo and right to redo; E3 stops at 0 and at the last action. If you undo and then make a new edit, the undone edits are replaced by the new one and the counter stays at the end. Edits made from a MIDI keyboard while holding a step count as edits too.

details.title: Counts and channels
details.text: The Memory screen also shows how many actions you can still undo and how many you can redo. Each channel has its own history, so a channel you have not edited shows an empty one.

title: Channel Length
summary: Set an independent inclusive channel range within the 64-step sequence.
prose:
Set channels independently, including the global scale pattern, within the 64-step sequence.

To set a channel range, hold its start step in Channel Editor. While holding the start, press and release a different, later end step, then release the start. The range commits when the end step is released. Brighter buttons indicate the active range.

The gesture cannot select a one-step range. A long hold alone has no effect; the held step remains available for combinations with other buttons, including a subsequent end-step press. The end must follow the start. A reversed selection shows a message and leaves the previous range unchanged. Channel ranges do not wrap from the final step to the first. The same restrictions apply to the Scale Editor range. Pattern note-length wrapping is unchanged.

Use the norns parameter [options](#options) to configure sequencer handling of channels with different lengths.

[Channel length demo](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=J1ckUZvhFJ0&t=2470s)

details.title: Range restrictions
details.text: Choose a different end step after the start. The two-key gesture cannot select a one-step range or wrap to an earlier end step. Holding a step alone does not change the range.

details.title: Setting two ranges
details.text: For channel 1 hold step 1 (grid (1,4)), tap and release step 16 ((16,4)), then release step 1. For channel 2 select it with (2,1), hold step 1, tap and release step 5 ((5,4)) and release step 1. Each channel needs notes to be heard. While one song pattern keeps playing, the ranges realign after the lowest common multiple of their lengths: 16 and 5 realign after 80 steps. A song pattern change resets the channels together unless Reset at Song Sequence Change is turned off in Options.

title: Muting Channels
summary: Toggle channel mute for the current song pattern by holding its selector or using K1.
prose:
Hold a channel-select button for one second to toggle that channel’s mute. Alternatively, hold K1 and press the channel-select button to toggle mute immediately. A muted channel button dims and, on a running channel, its notes stop and sounding notes are released. To bring the channel back while playing, hold K1 and tap its channel button; the button brightens and the phrase continues. If a channel is silent, check whether its button is dimmed.

Mute settings apply to the current song sequence, so different sequences can have different muted channels.

[Muting channels demo](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=J1ckUZvhFJ0&t=2687s)

title: Trig Parameters
summary: Assign up to ten parameters per channel and set defaults or step locks for the current song pattern.
prose:
Assign trig parameters to change sequencing or device sound values. Trig parameters belong to a song pattern, so different sections can use different parameter settings. Sequencer defaults such as Strum are saved with the project and restored per song pattern after loading; device patch values remain shared across patterns. Each channel has up to 10 assigned parameters. Set an individual [trig lock](#locks) on a step to override its parameter default. This per-step parameter method is also used on Elektron synthesizers.

The Trig params screen of the channel editor shows all ten slots at once. Each slot shows its parameter's two short names from the device definition, the first above the value and the second below, so together they name the parameter (for example `Quan` over `Note` for Quantised Fixed Note). The names stay still; one too long for its slot is cut short. A value too wide for its slot shows `...`, and while that slot is selected its full name and whole value take the last line. Use the following controls:

* **Screen Navigation**: Use E1 to open Channel tasks, then choose Masks, Trig params or another screen with E2 and open it with K3.
* **Changing Parameters**: To select a slot, turn E2. Adjust its value by rotating E3. To fine tune, rotate E3 whilst holding K1.
* **Activating Parameters**: To activate a different parameter within the same slot, press K2 to open the parameter list, turn E3 to browse, press K3 to assign, and press K2 to return.
* **Locking Changes**: As you adjust values, the system automatically saves your changes. You can also create "trig locks" on specific steps by holding down the step and turning E3. This allows you to set values that will override the default parameter for that step.
* **Default Parameter Values**: A pre-set parameter value is transmitted to your selected device on steps without a trig lock, unless the value is off or a parameter slide is active.
* **Handling Off Settings**: An explicit MIDI parameter lock set to "off" sends no value for that parameter on that step. It does not resend the previous lock or restore the default, so the device keeps its last received value. An off lock does not itself cancel a parameter slide that is already running; that slide may continue sending values.

[Params and trig locks demo](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=J1ckUZvhFJ0&t=2235s)

details.title: Fine adjustment
details.text: Hold K1 while turning E3 for fine adjustment on Trig params. For non-norns parameters with a range greater than 126, unshifted encoder input can use larger increments; K1 prevents that range-based acceleration. Norns parameters use their own parameter behaviour. This is not a guarantee that K1 changes the increment on every screen.

details.title: Off is not zero
details.text: An explicit Off lock on a step sends nothing for that parameter. It does not resend the previous lock or restore the default, so the device keeps the last value it received, and it is different from 0, which sends 0. An Off lock does not cancel a parameter slide that is already running; the slide may keep sending values.

details.title: Per song pattern
details.text: Sequencer trig params such as Strum, Arp and Probability keep their own channel settings in each song pattern; select a slot and the Trig params dials show that slot's values. Device sound params are shared by every song pattern, so a patch sounds the same in each section.

title: Sequencer Params
summary: Assign stock trig parameters that change sequencing rather than device sound parameters.
prose: All device types have a set of standard trig params that affect the sequencer rather than the quality of the sound.

title: Trig Probability
summary: Set a trig’s playback probability from 0 to 100, globally or per step.
prose: Set Trig Probability globally or per step. A value of 100 always plays the trig; 0 never plays it. A value of 50 gives it a fifty-percent playback probability.

details.title: Probability
details.text: A value of 50 gives each eligible trig a fifty-percent playback probability. It does not require exactly half the hits in a short loop to play. Set 0 for silence or 100 for certain playback.

title: Fixed Note
summary: Override ordinary root pitch with an unquantised MIDI note from 0 to 127.
prose: Set Fixed Note to a MIDI note number to override the channel’s ordinary root pitch. The note is not quantised. Use this parameter to hold a drum voice at its required MIDI note regardless of pattern note data. Fixed Note takes precedence over Quantised Fixed Note and random note values.

details.title: Note names on different screens
details.text: Compare numeric MIDI notes when moving between Fixed Note and Masks. Fixed Note’s label table starts MIDI 0 at C0 and labels MIDI 60 as C5. Masks uses norns musicutil and labels MIDI 60 as C3. The transmitted MIDI number is the same; this is an existing 1.4.0 display inconsistency.

title: Quantised Fixed Note
summary: Set MIDI pitch 0–127 and select the nearest playable pitch in the active scale. Ties choose the lower pitch.
prose: Quantised Fixed Note supplies an absolute MIDI pitch, 0–127, and selects the nearest playable note in the active scale at its configured root (or the song root when unset). Equally close notes select the lower pitch. The number includes its octave; channel/step octave, transposition, chord degree/rotation and pentatonic switches do not modify this override. It replaces pattern, note-mask and random pitch calculations for the ordinary root voice; separately generated chord/arp voices have their own processing. Fixed Note takes precedence. A step lock set to Off inherits the channel value; when both are Off, ordinary pitch processing resumes. Off does not silence the trig.

details.title: Why 63 can play 62
details.text: Quantised Fixed Note moves the number to the nearest note of the active scale. In C major 63 (D sharp) lies between 62 and 64; ties go to the lower note, so it plays 62. Fixed Note would play 63.

title: Random Note
summary: Add a random scale-degree offset. Zero leaves the note unchanged.
prose: Set Random Note to add a random offset to the selected note. A value of 0 will leave the note unchanged. A value of 1 will randomly give your existing note or the note one higher in the scale. A value of 2 will randomly give your existing note, the note one higher in your selected scale, or the note one lower. A value of 3 will randomly select notes -1, 0, 1 or 2. A value of 4 will randomly select notes -2, -1, 0, 1 or 2. Higher values continue this range expansion. Apply step locks where required. Random Note can be combined with Random Twos Note. By default, random notes are quantised to the pentatonic version of the currently selected scale to limit dissonant intervals. This can be disabled in _Mosaic_'s param settings. With Lock random to pent. enabled, a nonzero sum of Random Note and Random Twos offsets triggers nearest-pentatonic snapping for ordinary notes and fully quantised note masks, in either direction. Zero sums, including cancellation, do not trigger this option; other applicable pentatonic options still apply. Equal-distance pitches choose the lower note. Snap-only and unquantised masks retain their chromatic random-offset behaviour. Fixed Note and Quantised Fixed Note retain their override precedence.

details.title: How the value sets the range
details.text: Random Note n adds a random scale-degree offset. n = 1 gives 0 or +1, 2 gives -1 to +1, 3 gives -1 to +2 and 4 gives -2 to +2. Random Twos Note uses the same ranges in steps of two degrees. When both are set the offsets add, so 4 and 4 can move a note by up to 6 degrees either way. Each pass draws new offsets; the manual examples use a fixed seed so that they repeat exactly.

title: Random Twos Note
summary: Add a random offset in multiples of two scale degrees. Zero leaves the note unchanged.
prose: Set Random Twos Note to add a random offset restricted to multiples of two. A value of 0 will leave the note unchanged. A value of 1 will randomly give your existing note or the note two higher in the scale. A value of 2 will randomly give your existing note, the note two higher in your selected scale, or the note two lower. A value of 3 will randomly select notes -2, 0, 2 or 4. A value of 4 will randomly select notes -4, -2, 0, 2 or 4. Higher values continue this range expansion. Apply step locks where required. Random Twos Note can be combined with Random Note. By default, random notes are quantised to the pentatonic version of the currently selected scale to limit dissonant intervals. This can be disabled in _Mosaic_'s param settings. The Lock random to pent. rules described under Random Note apply to the sum of both params.

title: Chord Strum
summary: Play chord-mask slots once, spaced by the selected channel-step division.
prose: Use Strum to roll a chord from one voice to the next instead of sounding its voices together. First add chord masks on a polyphonic output, then assign Chord Note Strum in Trig params and set its division with E3. At 1/2, successive voices start half a channel step apart. X switches strumming off. Each chord voice plays once and follows the current scale, including a scale change during the roll.

details.title: Division values
details.text: Strum values are lengths in channel steps: 1/24 is the shortest and 128 the longest; X switches strumming off. Turning E3 down stops at X and turning it up stops at 128. 1/2 puts half a step between successive chord notes. Each chord note starts at its strum time and then lasts the note length from its own start.

details.title: Empty voices and timing
details.text: Chord Shape orders the root and four chord-mask slots. Empty slots keep their positions and consume spacing and acceleration ordinals, including trailing empty slots. The advanced sparse-chord examples show these rests; start with the five-voice timed chord to learn the basic roll.

title: Chord Arpeggio
summary: Repeat chord slots at the selected division for the note’s duration. Arpeggio takes precedence over Strum.
prose:
Set Chord Arp to repeat the chord-mask slots at the selected step division for the current note’s length. Notes are quantised to the current scale. Empty chord masks are treated as rests, allowing for rhythmic patterns. Arpeggios also honour the Chord Velocity and Chord Shape modifiers. The Chord Arpeggio param overrules the chord strum param. Chord arpeggios can also be used as ratchets if no chord masks are set.

With Chord Spread at zero, the first arp interval is one full selected division of the channel step. For example, a half-step arp on a two-step note advances through its slots at 0, 1/2, 1 and 1 1/2 steps; it does not start another note at the two-step endpoint. Each arp note lasts one selected division from its own onset, shortened when necessary to finish at the original note's endpoint.

Starting another arp on the same channel cancels the old arp's future notes. Notes already sounding keep their remaining duration, capped by their original endpoint; the old arp's endpoint does not cut notes from its replacement. Pattern resets likewise preserve the remaining duration of sounding notes. Stop releases sounding notes and cancels future arp notes. Overlapping notes of the same MIDI pitch still send a corresponding Note Off for each Note On; how a receiving instrument handles overlapping voices is unchanged.

Chord Shape orders the root and four chord-mask slots. An empty mask slot, or a muted root slot, is a rest and keeps its position, including at the end of the sequence. Rest slots consume the same time and acceleration ordinal as sounding slots. If no chord masks are populated, an unmuted root instead forms a one-slot ratchet; if the root is also muted, the result is silence.

details.title: Division values
details.text: Arpeggio values are lengths in channel steps: 1/24 is the shortest and 128 the longest; X switches the arpeggio off. 1/2 repeats the chord slots at half-step intervals for the length of the note. Turning E3 down stops at X and turning it up stops at 128, as on the Chord Strum page.

title: Chord Acceleration
summary: Change successive Strum or Arpeggio gaps using Spread and Acceleration. Zero Spread disables the acceleration effect.
prose:
Chord Acceleration modifies the spacing of an enabled Strum or Arpeggio together with Chord Spread. Off (0) means no progressive change: every gap is the selected division plus Spread. A positive value lengthens each following gap; a negative value shortens it. With Spread at zero, Acceleration has no effect.

In channel-step units, let `d` be the Strum or Arp division, `s` be Spread, and `a` be Acceleration (zero when off). The gap before slot `k`, counting the first gap as 1, is `d + s * (1 + (k - 1) * a)`. The first slot occurs at trigger time; later slot times are the sums of these gaps. A new trigger restarts the ordinal. Wrapping an arp's slots does not restart it. These are the nominal musical times before swing and clock-pulse quantisation. An arp interval occupies at least one scheduler pulse, including after swing. At fast channel rates, this limits the resolution of very short gaps.

For a division of 1/2 and Spread of 1/4:

| Acceleration | Successive gaps | Slot times from the trigger |
|---|---|---|
| Off | 3/4, 3/4, 3/4, 3/4 | 0, 3/4, 3/2, 9/4, 3 |
| +1 | 3/4, 1, 5/4, 3/2 | 0, 3/4, 7/4, 3, 9/2 |
| +2 | 3/4, 5/4, 7/4, 9/4 | 0, 3/4, 2, 15/4, 6 |
| -1 | 3/4, 1/2, 1/4, then 0 | 0, 3/4, 5/4, 3/2, then stop |

When the next gap is zero or negative, scheduling ends before that slot. There is no extra simultaneous note or reversed time; notes already sounding retain their releases. Empty slots, including trailing rests, advance the same ordinal in both strums and arps.

details.title: Worked example: a strum that stops early
details.text: Fill only Chd1 and Chd4, set Chord Pattern to reverse (<-), Strum to 1/2, Spread to 1/4 and Chord Accel Mod to -1. The order is slot 4, 3, 2, 1, root. Slot 4 sounds at once; slot 3 is empty and follows 3/4 step later; slot 2 is empty and follows 1/2 step after that; slot 1 sounds 1/4 step after that, 1 1/2 steps after the trigger. The gap before the root would be 0, so the root never sounds.

title: Chord Spread
summary: Add a channel-step duration to Strum or Arpeggio spacing without changing note length.
prose: Chord Spread adds a duration to the selected Strum or Arp division, measured in channel steps. For example, a half-step division with quarter-step Spread starts with a three-quarter-step gap. With Acceleration off, all gaps stay at that value. With Acceleration enabled, each following gap changes by Spread multiplied by Acceleration, as above. Spacing modifiers act only when Strum or Arpeggio is enabled and do not change the selected note length. Arp notes remain limited by their original note endpoint.

details.title: Division values
details.text: Spread values are lengths in channel steps from 1/24 to 128; X adds nothing. Turning E3 down stops at X and turning it up stops at 128, as on the Chord Strum page. Strum 1/2 plus Spread 1/4 puts 3/4 of a step between chord notes.

title: Chord Velocity Modifier
summary: Adjust successive chord-note velocities by a positive or negative increment.
prose: Set Chord Velocity Modifier to change successive chord-note velocities by an increment, starting from the root note. Positive values make the chord swell, each note louder than the one before; negative values make it fade.

details.title: Compare dynamics, not just pitches
details.text: The ordinal example uses a five-voice chord whose velocities rise 50, 60, 70, 80, 90. Keep the chord pitches fixed while comparing the accents. Restore the modifier to Off to remove this progressive dynamic change.

title: Chord Shape Modifier
summary: Set the slot order used by Chord Strum and Chord Arpeggio.
prose: Set Chord Shape Modifier to change the chord-mask slot order used by Chord Strum and Chord Arpeggio.

details.title: Orders
details.text: -> plays the root then chord slots 1-4. <- reverses the order: it plays slots 4-1 then the root. X applies no shape: the root plays first. With no strum the voices start together, so a shape matters most with Strum or Arpeggio. A step lock set to X returns that step to root-first. -><- alternates between the start and the end of that order, working inward: root, slot 4, slot 1, slot 3, slot 2. <--> does the same starting from the end: slot 4, root, slot 3, slot 1, slot 2.

title: Mute Root Note
summary: Silence the chord’s root slot while retaining its other chord voices.
prose: Enable Mute Root Note to omit the root of a chord while retaining its other chord voices. Use this parameter to change a chord voicing or inversion.

details.title: Time slots stay
details.text: Mute Chord Root leaves the root slot silent without moving the other voices: with Strum 1/2 the chord notes stay at 1/2, 1, 1 1/2 and 2 steps after the trigger.

title: Fully Quantise Mask
summary: Set whether note masks follow scale degree and rotation, overriding global quantisation when explicitly Off or On.
prose: The Fully Quantise Mask param controls whether note masks on a step are fully quantised to the current scale, including scale degree and rotation adjustments. On maps written note masks through the scale, including Degree and Rotation. Off leaves full mapping disabled; the separate Snap note masks to scale option may still snap accidentals. Set this parameter per channel or step to override global quantisation. Channel X uses the global Quantise note masks setting; explicit Off and On override it. An explicit step X uses the global setting directly, bypassing the channel value. Clearing that step lock instead restores the channel value (and therefore the global setting if the channel is X).

details.title: How the three levels combine
details.text: A step On or Off overrides the channel. With no step lock, the channel applies; channel X follows the global Quantise note masks option. An explicitly stored step X instead uses the global option directly, skipping the channel. Clearing that step with K2 restores channel inheritance. Choose On to make note masks follow Degree and Rotation; choose Off to disable full mapping. Snap note masks to scale is a separate option, so Off does not by itself guarantee chromatic notes.

title: Scale Editor
summary: Choose the scale the song plays in. Edit any of the 16 scale slots (Root, Scale, Degree, Transpose, Rotation) without changing playback until you apply it.
prose:
The Scale Editor sets the harmony of the whole song and holds 16 scale slots. Changing the scale changes the pitches that pattern degrees produce; it does not change rhythm or pattern degrees.

Apply a scale:

1. Press Grid (4, 8) to open the Scale Editor. The scale slots are the 16 buttons on Grid row 3. The applied slot is brightly lit.
2. Short-press a slot. It is applied to every channel and selected for editing.
3. To turn global scale off, short-press the applied slot again. The slot stays selected for editing. With global scale off and no scale lock, pattern degrees play as chromatic semitone offsets. Press the slot again to apply it.

A pattern uses the applied scale unless a global scale lock or a channel scale lock overrides it.

Edit a slot:

1. Turn E2 to select Root, Scale, Degree, Transpose or Rotation. Scale tasks are Scale, Scale clock and Overview.
2. Turn E3 to change the value of the selected row. The title row names the slot you are editing.
3. Release all grid keys, then press K3 to apply the changes or K2 to cancel. Tapping any grid key, including Play/Stop, cancels an unapplied edit, so press K3 first.

Edit a slot without playing it:

1. Hold K1 and press the slot, or long-press a slot that is not selected for editing.
2. Edit the slot as above and press K3. Playback does not change. A dim indicator marks the editing slot when it differs from the applied slot.
3. Long-press the slot already selected for editing to turn global scale off and clear the editing selection.

Applying changes to the slot that is playing changes the sound immediately.

Set a scale lock: hold a step and press a scale slot. On the Scale page the lock is global for channels without a channel scale lock; on a channel page it applies to that channel. See [Scale Locks](#scale-locks).

The global scale track has its own rate and length, so a chord progression can run over a different number of steps from the patterns. On the Scale clock task, E2 selects Rate and E3 changes it; K3 applies. The same screen shows the selected range, the global cap and the playable range as read-only values. To change the length, hold the first step of the range on the scale track and press its last step. The end must come after the start: a reversed selection is rejected with the tooltip End must follow start and the previous range stays, and ranges do not wrap from the last step back to the first.

Video: [Scale editor demo](https://youtu.be/J1ckUZvhFJ0?t=2741)

details.title: Editing selection and applied scale
details.text: The title row names the slot selected for editing. The editing indicator is dim when that slot differs from the applied scale. With global scale off and no scale lock, pattern degrees play as chromatic semitone offsets. An active channel scale lock takes precedence over the global scale.

details.title: Vertical list controls
details.text: Scale settings appear as vertical rows. Turn E2 to select a row and bring later fields into view. E3 edits the selected slot's draft; K3 applies it and K2 cancels it. Selecting another row does not apply a draft. Tapping a grid key, including Play/Stop, cancels an unapplied draft, so press K3 before using the grid to keep your edit. A long scale name uses a separate full-width value row.

details.title: Scale lock lifetime
details.text: A global scale lock lasts until another global lock or until the global scale track wraps. A channel scale lock follows PARAMS > MOSAIC > Scales lock until ptn end, which is On by default. See Scale Locks.

details.title: Scale clock and Overview
details.text: Scale clock sets the rate of the global scale track. Overview is a read-only dashboard: it lists the playing scale, the scale being edited, the step range, the transposition and any step lock. Both are Scale tasks beside Scale.

recipes.title: Prepare and apply a second scale

title: Transposition
summary: Transpose the whole selected Song Sequence by -12 to +12 semitones with one fader. Locks change it from chosen steps.
prose:
Use the transposition fader on the Scale page to transpose every channel of the selected Song Sequence without editing any note. Rhythm and intervals stay the same.

Set global transposition:

1. Press Grid (4, 8) to open the Scale Editor.
2. Press a button on the transposition fader, Grid row 8, columns 8–16. The tooltip shows Transpose and the new value.

The fader buttons set these values: (9,8) is -12, (10,8) -8, (11,8) -4, (12,8) 0, (13,8) +4, (14,8) +8 and (15,8) +12. The end buttons, (8,8) and (16,8), lower or raise the value by one semitone each press.

The global value is added to the active scale slot's Transpose value. With scale slot 1 as C major and the melody 60, 62, 64, 65, +2 plays 62, 64, 66, 67.

You can change transposition while playing. A note that is already sounding keeps its pitch and length. The next notes use the new value.

To change transposition from a certain step onwards, use [transposition locks](#transposition-locks).

Video: [Global transposition demo](https://youtu.be/J1ckUZvhFJ0?t=2905)

details.title: Transposition precedence
details.text: The current global value, or the persistent step-lock value, is added to the active scale slot's Transpose value. For its lifetime, a step lock replaces the global fader value.

details.title: Each Song slot has its own transposition
details.text: Transposition belongs to the selected Song Sequence. Copying a Song slot copies its transposition, and changing the copy leaves the original as it was.

details.title: Edits during playback
details.text: A change made while notes sound does not cut the sounding note or change its length. The next onset uses the new value. In the captured example, +1 and then -12 raise the following notes by one semitone and then drop them an octave from the written pitch.

recipes.title: Play a copied Song slot a tone higher

title: Song Editor
summary: Select and arrange 96 Song Sequence slots on six grid rows. Each slot stores its pattern, channel and harmonic setup.
prose:
The Song Editor contains 96 Song Sequence slots, arranged in six rows of 16. Slot 1 is grid (1,1), slot 2 is (2,1), slot 16 is (16,1), slot 17 is (1,2) and slot 96 is (16,6). Each slot stores one complete sequence: which patterns each channel plays, merge modes, masks, scales, mutes and the sequence length. Use a slot for each section of a song.

Press Song, grid (6,8), to open the editor. The norns shows Song Playback. Fill slots by copying a finished section into a new slot and editing the copy (see Interacting with Slots). Read slot brightness in Button Indicators. Let Song mode chain slots automatically with Song Mode Operations. Set how many steps a section plays with the fader on row 7 (Adjusting Song Sequence Length).

Watch: [Song editor demo](https://youtu.be/J1ckUZvhFJ0?t=2972)

details.title: Song slot contents
details.text: Copying a Song slot copies its sequence configuration. Source note patterns and channel settings can be reused or changed within the copied slot.

recipes.title: Create a two-slot group

title: Button Indicators
summary: Song slot brightness indicates empty, filled and selected slots.
prose:
Read Song slot status from the grid. The slots fill rows 1 to 6.

* Dim buttons indicate empty slots.
* Mid-glow buttons indicate slots containing rhythms and patterns.
* The brightly lit button identifies the Song Sequence that is selected, or playing.
* A slot you pressed during playback blinks (its light pulses down and back up) until the current sequence finishes and the slot takes over.

Example: copy slot 1 to slot 2 and select slot 2. Slot 1 is mid-bright, slot 2 is bright and slot 3 is dim. Press Play and slot 2 stays bright. Press slot 1 while slot 2 plays: slot 1 blinks until slot 2 finishes, then slot 1 turns bright and slot 2 returns to mid-bright. Copy empty slot 3 over slot 2 while stopped and slot 2 goes dim.

details.title: Selected while stopped
details.text: The bright indicator represents the selected Song slot, including when transport is stopped. During playback it identifies the current section; queued selection has blinking feedback.

title: Interacting with Slots
summary: Select, copy and erase Song slots using grid presses.
prose:
Press a slot button to select its Song Sequence. Slot 1 is grid (1,1), slot 2 is (2,1), slot 16 is (16,1) and slot 17 is (1,2). While stopped, the press selects the slot at once and the norns shows Slot setup for it. During playback, the press queues the slot until the current sequence finishes.

To copy a slot, press and hold the source slot, press the destination slot, then release both. The destination becomes a full copy of the source. Editing the copy leaves the source untouched. The destination’s previous contents are overwritten, so copy onto an empty slot unless you mean to replace it.

To erase a slot, copy an empty slot over it: hold the empty slot and press the slot to clear. There is no undo.

details.title: Copy direction
details.text: Press the source slot first, then the destination. Either release order uses the first-pressed slot as the source. Copying leaves the source and other slots unchanged.

title: Song Mode Operations
summary: Song mode advances to the next filled slot after the current slot’s repeats. An empty slot ends the contiguous group and returns playback to that group’s first filled slot.
prose:
Song mode plays your slots as an arrangement. It is on by default. With Song mode on, the sequencer advances to the next filled slot after the current slot has played its Repeats. Turn it on or off in Song tasks > Slot setup (select Song mode with E2, set it with E3, apply with K3) or in PARAMS > MOSAIC > Song mode.

A run of filled slots with no gap is a group. When playback reaches an empty slot, it returns to the first filled slot of its group. Slots 1 and 2 with slot 3 empty therefore play 1, 2, 1, 2 and so on. Use empty slots to separate groups.

Press another slot during playback to queue a change. The slot blinks, and the change takes effect after the current sequence, including its repeats, completes. This is how you move from one group to another.

With Song mode off, slots do not advance by themselves: the selected slot keeps repeating. A queued manual selection still takes over at the end of the current sequence.

details.title: Song groups
details.text: When the next slot is empty, playback returns to the first filled slot of the current contiguous group. Manual slot selection remains available when Song mode is off.

details.title: How long a slot lasts
details.text: A slot plays its global length in steps, once for every repeat, before Song mode advances. Set the length with the fader on row 7 and Repeats in Slot setup.

recipes.title: Create two Song groups

title: Adjusting Song Sequence Length
summary: Set the selected Song Sequence’s global length from 1 to 64 steps. Each track plays at most this number of steps, counted from its own start.
prose:
Use the fader at the lower left of the Song Editor to set the global length of the selected Song Sequence from 1 to 64 steps. It is on row 7, columns 1 to 8. Press Song (6,8) to open the editor. A press on the fader opens Song Playback on the norns, where Global length shows the new value.

* (1,7) subtracts one step. (8,7) adds one step.
* The inner buttons jump to a coarse value: (2,7) sets 1, (3,7) sets 13, (4,7) sets 32, (5,7) sets 38, (6,7) sets 51 and (7,7) sets 64.
* To reach an exact value, jump to a nearby coarse value and finish with the end buttons. For 16, tap (3,7) and then (8,7) three times.

Channel start and end steps may lie outside the global-length range. A channel’s played length cannot exceed global length. The limit counts steps from the channel start: with channel range 2–4 and global length 2, playback repeats steps 2 and 3. Increase global length to restore the remaining selected steps.

The same limit applies to the scale track. Each track follows its own clock rate, and explicit song reset options still apply.

Watch: [Global pattern length demo](https://youtu.be/J1ckUZvhFJ0?t=3160)

details.title: Global length and channel range
details.text: With channel range 2–4 and global length 2, the channel repeats steps 2 and 3. Its selected endpoint remains at 4. Increasing global length restores step 4. The scale track follows the same length cap. Each track retains its clock rate, and explicit song reset options still apply.

recipes.title: Shorten and restore a phrase

title: Navigating the Norns Display
summary: Open Playback, Slot setup or Tempo / feel from Song tasks.
prose:
The Song page opens on Playback. This read-only screen shows the playing slot (Playing), the slot that follows (Next, or HOLD when Song mode is off), the current pass within its repeats (Pass, for example 1 / 2), the global pattern length and whether Song mode is advancing (AUTO) or off (MANUAL). Turn E1 to open Song tasks: Playback, Slot setup, Tempo / feel and Channel view.

Open Slot setup to set Repeats, the number of passes the selected Song Sequence plays before Song mode advances, and to see Song mode. With Song mode off, select slots manually.

Open Tempo / feel (the screen is titled GLOBAL FEEL) to set the global tempo and Swing or Shuffle. The tempo is shared by every slot.

Channel view opens the same screen as in Pattern tasks: the viewed channel on its own.

details.title: Setting scope
details.text: Repeats applies to the selected Song slot. Song mode, tempo and global feel apply across the song.

details.title: Vertical list controls
details.text: Slot setup and Tempo / feel use vertical lists. Turn E2 to select the row and E3 to edit it. K3 applies the draft; K2 cancels. Repeats belongs to the selected slot; Song mode and global feel apply across the song. Playback remains a read-only dashboard.

details.title: Set Repeats for a slot
details.text: Select the slot on the grid. Turn E1 to Song tasks, turn E2 to Slot setup and press K3. Repeats is the first row and is already selected. Turn E3 to the new value, for example 2, and press K3 to apply. Song mode uses Repeats to decide when to advance; with Song mode off the value appears as the pass count on Playback.

details.title: Set the tempo
details.text: Turn E1 to Song tasks, turn E2 to Tempo / feel and press K3. Tempo is the selected row. Turn E3 to the required value, from 30 to 300 BPM, and press K3 to apply. Because tempo is global, every slot then reads and plays the same tempo.

title: Locks
summary: Store a different value on one step. Hold the step, then change the same control you use for the whole channel.
prose:
A lock stores a value on one step, so that step differs from the channel default. Hold the step on the grid, change the value, then release the step. The lock stays in place and the screen returns to the channel default.

Each lock type has its own control:

1. Parameter lock: on Channel tasks > Trig params, hold a step and turn E3. See [Trig Param Locks](#trig-param-locks).
2. Mask lock: on Channel tasks > Masks, hold a step and turn E3. See [Mask Locks](#mask-locks).
3. Octave lock: hold a step and press an octave button on Grid row 8, columns 8–12. See [Octave Locks](#octave-locks).
4. Scale lock: hold a step and press a scale slot on Grid row 3. On a channel page the lock affects that channel. On the Scale page it is global. See [Scale Locks](#scale-locks).
5. Transposition lock: on the Scale page, hold a scale-track step and press the transposition fader on Grid row 8. See [Transposition Locks](#transposition-locks).

Parameter, mask and octave locks change their own step only. A transposition lock stays in force on the steps that follow it until a later transposition lock replaces it. A channel scale lock lasts as set by Scales lock until ptn end (see [Scale Locks](#scale-locks)). A global scale lock lasts until another global lock replaces it or the scale track wraps.

To remove a lock, hold its step and press K2 on the screen where you set it. For octave, scale and transposition locks you can also press the same button again.

details.title: Evidence: transpose output scope
details.text: The held-step readout establishes the explicit zero value. The intermediate MIDI stream is truncated and is not evidence of a complete phrase. The final clear checkpoint includes the complete phrase and preserves step 2’s separate zero lock.

Compare a stored device value with one step-local CC lock
