title: Trig Param Locks
summary: Give one step its own value for an assigned device parameter, such as filter cutoff.
prose:
Before you set a parameter lock, assign the parameter to one of the ten Trig params slots (see [Trig Parameters](#trig-parameters)). The value you set with no step held is the channel default that every step sends.

Set a parameter lock:

1. Open Trig params from Channel tasks with E1.
2. Turn E2 to select the assigned slot.
3. Hold a step on the channel sequencer.
4. Turn E3 to the value for that step. While the step is held, the cell shows the held value and an L marker.
5. Release the step. The cell shows the channel default again; the step keeps its lock.

Clear a step's parameter trig locks:

1. Open Trig params.
2. Hold the step and press K2.

Clear all parameter trig locks on the channel:

1. Open Trig params.
2. Release all steps.
3. Hold K1 and press K2.

Video: [Trig locks demo](https://youtu.be/J1ckUZvhFJ0?t=2235)

details.title: Ten slots
details.text: Each channel has ten Trig params slots. Turn E2 to move between them; it stops at slot 1 and at slot 10. Each slot keeps its own default and its own step locks, and the scene below assigns CC 1 to CC 10 and locks one step on slot 10 and another on slot 1.

details.title: Clearing is per step
details.text: Hold the step and press K2 on Trig params clears every parameter lock on that step, not only the selected slot.

details.title: Independent comparisons
details.text: The pitch-lock example uses Fixed Note to demonstrate default, exception and clear. The cutoff recipe uses CC 74 and needs a receiver that maps that controller to its filter. The Decay audio comparison is a separate sound-design extension, and the chord/strum recording demonstrates different controls. Use the CC value comparison to check this recipe.

recipes.title: Brighten the last note with a cutoff lock

title: Param Slides
summary: Make a parameter move gradually from one lock to the next instead of jumping.
prose:
A slide needs at least two parameter locks of the same parameter on the channel. Set them first (see [Trig Param Locks](#trig-param-locks)).

Slide a parameter across the whole channel:

1. Open Trig params and select the parameter with E2.
2. Release all steps and press K3. The cell shows S.

Between every pair of locks of that parameter the value now moves gradually. Press K3 again with no step held to switch it off.

Slide from one step only:

1. Hold the step that has the lock you want to slide from.
2. With the parameter selected, press K3.

The held step slides to the next lock of that parameter. Other locks of the parameter still jump.

Slides do not cross into a different song pattern. Turn on Wrap param slides to let the last lock of a repeating pattern slide back to the first lock (see [Parameter Slides Wrap](#parameter-slides-wrap)). Slides use extra processing, so use them only where you need them.

Video: [Param slides demo](https://youtu.be/iGx5fmrbatA?t=515)

recipes.title: Open a filter over two steps

title: Mask Locks
summary: Give one step its own note, velocity, length or other mask value. Step locks override the channel default masks.
prose:
A mask has a channel default and, for each step, an optional step lock. With no step held, E3 changes the channel default. With a step held, E3 changes the lock on that step only.

Set a mask lock:

1. Open Masks from Channel tasks with E1.
2. Turn E2 to the mask you want, for example Note or Vel.
3. Hold a step on the channel sequencer.
4. Turn E3 to the value for that step.
5. Release the step. The screen shows the channel default again; the step keeps its lock.

Clear a step's mask locks:

1. Open Masks.
2. Hold the step and press K2.

Clear all step-mask locks on the channel:

1. Open Masks.
2. Release all steps.
3. Hold K1 and press K2.
Channel default masks are retained.

Video: [Mask locks demo](https://youtu.be/J1ckUZvhFJ0?t=1780)

details.title: Example
details.text: With a channel velocity of 50, hold step 1 and turn E3 to 90. Step 1 plays at velocity 90 and the other steps play at 50. Holding step 1 and pressing K2 returns it to 50.

details.title: X and zero
details.text: X means no mask: the step inherits the pattern's value. A velocity of 0 is a mask that silences the step. The two are different.

recipes.title: Make one step override a channel Note default, then restore inheritance
Contrast inherited velocity with explicit zero and a cleared exception

title: Scale Locks
summary: Change the scale on a step, for one channel or for every channel. A channel lock overrides the global scale.
prose:
Scale slots are the 16 buttons on Grid row 3. A scale lock applies a slot from a chosen step. Set it on a channel page for that channel only, or on the Scale page for every channel that has no channel scale lock.

Set a channel scale lock:

1. Select the channel and hold a step on the channel sequencer.
2. Press the required scale slot on Grid row 3. The norns screen shows Scale source.

Set a global scale lock:

1. Press Grid (4, 8) to open the Scale Editor.
2. Hold a step on the scale track and press the required scale slot on Grid row 3. The norns screen shows Scale overview.

Clear a step lock:

1. Hold the step.
2. Press K2, or press the same scale slot again.

A channel scale lock overrides the global scale and global locks.

With Scales lock until ptn end On (the default), a channel scale lock lasts until the channel wraps to its start or another channel scale lock replaces it.

With the option Off, the lock lasts until the next active trig that passes its probability check. A trig that fails its probability check does not clear it. A scale lock on the next accepted trig replaces the previous lock.

Global scale-track locks ignore this option. They last until another global lock replaces them or the global scale track wraps.

Video: [Scale locks demo](https://youtu.be/J1ckUZvhFJ0?t=2854)

details.title: Scale source screen
details.text: After a channel scale lock, Scale source lists the channel lock, the global lock, the selected scale and the effective scale. Use it to see which lock is winning. It is read-only.

title: Transposition Locks
summary: Transpose the song from a chosen scale-track step. The lock is added to the selected scale's Transpose value.
prose:
Transposition locks belong to the global scale track on the Scale page. Reach the Scale page from the Channel editor with Grid (4,8) and set the lock on a scale-track step there, not on a channel step.

Set a transposition lock:

1. Press Grid (4, 8) to open the Scale Editor.
2. Hold a step on the scale track.
3. Press the required value on the transposition fader, Grid row 8, columns 8–16.
4. Release the step. The norns screen shows Scale overview.

From that step, the lock replaces the global transposition fader value. It is added to the selected scale's own Transpose value. It stays in force on the following steps until a later transposition lock replaces it.

A lock of 0 is a real lock. It cancels the global transposition from that step. It is not the same as having no lock.

Clear a transposition lock:

1. Hold the step on the Scale page.
2. Press K2, or press the same fader value again.

details.title: Fader values
details.text: Pressing a fader button sets a value: (9,8) -12, (10,8) -8, (11,8) -4, (12,8) 0, (13,8) +4, (14,8) +8 and (15,8) +12. The end buttons (8,8) and (16,8) step down or up by one semitone each press.

details.title: Example
details.text: Global transposition is +4 and the melody is 60, 62, 64, 65. A lock of 0 on scale-track step 2 plays steps 2 to 4 untransposed (62, 64, 65). A lock of +12 on step 1 makes the first note 72. Clearing the lock on step 1 returns it to the global +4, so it plays 64.

title: Octave Locks
summary: Place one step in a different octave from the channel's octave.
prose:
Set an octave lock:

1. Hold a step on the channel sequencer.
2. Press an octave button on Grid row 8, columns 8–12: (8,8) is -2, (9,8) is -1, (10,8) is 0, (11,8) is +1 and (12,8) is +2.
3. Release the step.

With no step held, the same five buttons set the channel octave. A step's octave lock replaces the channel octave for that step. With the channel at -2, a lock of 0 puts that step back at its written octave, two octaves above its neighbours.

Clear an octave lock:

1. Hold the step.
2. Press K2 on Trig params, or press the same octave button again.

title: Save and Load
summary: Save named projects and load saved projects from PARAMS > MOSAIC. Stopped, idle projects normally autosave after 60 seconds.
prose:
Save a named project:

1. Press K1 to open PARAMS and choose MOSAIC.
2. Choose Save project.
3. Enter a descriptive name on the text entry screen and press K3 to confirm. The suggested name is new.

Mosaic writes a project file (.ptn) and a parameter file under that name. Saving under a name that already exists replaces that save. Press K2 in the dialog to cancel; no file changes.

Load a project: open PARAMS > MOSAIC, choose Load, pick the file in the file picker and press K3.

Use named saves for versions that autosave must not overwrite. When playback is stopped, 60 seconds of inactivity normally saves the current project as autosave. Mosaic loads the most recent autosave at startup. Named saves are separate files and autosave does not change them.

Before replacing the current project, Mosaic checks saved song slots, global lengths, channel ranges and scale-track ranges. If a check fails, the screen identifies the problem. The current project and playback are retained.

A rejected load suspends autosave to protect the rejected file. Editing, playing and cancelling a dialog do not resume autosave. A successful valid load, a successful named save or New resumes the normal idle autosave interval. A failed save leaves autosave suspended.

Valid saved one-step ranges are supported. There is no one-step range gesture. Validation covers the saved range structure; it does not check every possible corrupted project field.

details.title: Enter a name: separate arrangement demonstration
details.text:
Open [Enter a project name and keep the arrangement](#save-and-load/lesson/save-named-arrangement) for the complete name-entry demonstration. The sequencer is stopped with SONG 01 selected. This separate demonstration loads a copy of the finished course arrangement and opens Slot setup through the public Song grid control. It begins with the first Save attempt already cancelled and < Save project selected. It is not a continuation of the original course recording.

1. Stop playback and select SONG 01. Open the Song editor with its grid control. Turn E1 clockwise to open Song tasks, select Slot setup with E2 and press K3. SLOT SETUP / SONG 01 is the starting screen.
2. Press K1, open PARAMS > MOSAIC and select Save project with E2. Press K3 to open name entry. Press K2 to cancel this first attempt. The Save project menu returns without creating a named file.
3. Press K3 to open name entry again. The suggested name is new, with OK selected.
4. Turn E2 left to DEL. Press K3 three times to remove the suggested name. The name is empty.
5. Turn E3 left to the character row. Turn E2 until F is the bright character, then press K3. F appears in the name.
6. Select o, u and r with E2, pressing K3 after each character. Select the blank space and press K3. Select n, o, t, e and s in the same way. The name reads Four notes.
7. Turn E3 right to the DEL / OK row, then turn E2 right to OK. Press K3 to save. Press K1 to return to Mosaic. SLOT SETUP / SONG 01 returns.
8. Press K1 to return to PARAMS > MOSAIC. Select Load project with E2 and press K3. Turn E2 until Four notes.ptn is selected. This confirms that the named project is available; leave it selected without loading a different project.
9. Press K2 to cancel the picker, then K1 to return to Mosaic. The same arrangement remains open.

Saved Four notes: the named project retains the complete decoded arrangement and its parameter file. Four notes.ptn is available in the Load picker; cancelling the picker leaves SLOT SETUP / SONG 01 open.

Saving under an existing name replaces that save. Use a distinct name when retaining an earlier version. If loading leaves the norns tasks unresponsive, tap the Song editor grid control before opening Song tasks; the demonstration uses this explicit public starting navigation.

title: Options
summary: Configure Mosaic from PARAMS > MOSAIC: playback, parameter locks, quantiser, MIDI keyboard and screen settings.
prose:
Mosaic keeps its settings in the norns PARAMS menu, not on the grid. Tap K1 to open the norns menu, choose PARAMS, then choose MOSAIC. Turn E2 to move between rows and turn E3 to change the selected value. Changes take effect at once; there is no apply step. Press K2 to step back and K1 to close the menu.

The MOSAIC list also holds the project actions (save, load, new). The settings are grouped as Sequencer, Parameter locks, Quantiser, Midi control and Screen. Every option is described in its own section below with its default, and every option starts at that default in a new project.

details.title: Where each option lives
details.text: Sequencer: Shift press to stop, Song mode, Reset on song seq change, Reset on pattern repeat, Wrap param slides, Elektron program changes and Elektron p.change channel. Parameter locks: Lock lead time and Trigless locks. Quantiser: Snap note masks to scale, Quantise note masks, Scales lock until ptn end, Lock all to pent., Lock random to pent. and Lock merged to pent. Midi control: Map scale to white keys and the Honour switches. Screen: UI motion.

recipes.title: Prepare Mosaic for a live set

title: Sequencer Options
summary: Set stop protection, song progression, resets, slide wrapping and program changes.
prose: Open PARAMS > MOSAIC and scroll to the Sequencer options. They decide how playback starts and stops, how the song moves between slots and what each slot change or repeat does to the channels, how a slide behaves at the loop end, and whether Mosaic sends program changes to a receiver. Turn E2 to a row and turn E3 to change it.

details.title: Defaults
details.text: Shift press to stop Off. Song mode On. Reset on song seq change On. Reset on pattern repeat Off. Wrap param slides Off. Elektron program changes Off, on channel 10.

details.title: Which lesson to read
details.text: Stopping safely: Shift press stop. Song sections: Song mode and the two reset options, read in that order. Slides across the loop end: Parameter slides wrap. Syncing a pattern-based receiver: Elektron program changes.

recipes.title: Arrange sections that restart together

title: Shift press stop
summary: Require K1 or a long press to stop playback. Default: Off.
prose:
Shift press to stop protects a performance from an accidental stop. With it On, a short tap on Play/Stop (grid (1,8)) no longer stops playback. Starting playback is not affected: a tap still starts it. To stop, hold K1 and tap Play/Stop, or hold Play/Stop for one second or more. A hold of 0.9 seconds is too short and is ignored. Holding K3 while tapping does not count as shift.

With the option Off, a tap on Play/Stop stops playback, as in an ordinary project.

details.title: What is protected
details.text: Only stopping is protected. A tap starts playback in either setting.

recipes.title: Play a set without accidental stops

title: Song Mode
summary: Advance through the song sequence automatically. Default: On.
prose:
Song mode is On by default. With Song mode On, the song steps through its slots on its own, according to the Song Editor's global length and the groups of slots you filled. Playback moves from one slot to the next when the current slot reaches its global length, and a group of slots loops.

With Song mode Off, Mosaic keeps playing the selected slot and moves only when you select another slot yourself. Use Off to rehearse a single section or to move between sections by hand. Song mode also decides whether the repeat reset in Reset on pattern repeat applies: with Song mode Off, a repeating slot is not reset.

recipes.title: Rehearse one section

title: Reset at Song Editor Pattern Change
summary: Reset channel positions when the song pattern changes. Default: On.
prose:
Reset on song seq change is On by default. With On, every channel restarts from its first step at the moment the Song Editor moves to a different slot, so each section starts together. With Off, channels carry on from where they were, including channels whose length does not divide the section.

The difference shows with a slow channel. Take a three-step channel at Clock Mod /9 (one step every 1.5 seconds) in a song whose slots are 64 steps long (10.7 seconds). With Off, the notes carry across the slot change. With On, the channel's first note sounds exactly at the change.

recipes.title: Hear the section restart

title: Reset at Pattern Repeat
summary: Reset channel positions when the song pattern repeats. Default: Off.
prose:
Reset on pattern repeat is Off by default. With On and Song mode On, every channel returns to its first step when the same song slot repeats at the end of its global length. A channel with its own length or clock rate therefore starts its phrase again on each repeat. With Off, the channel's phase carries across the repeat, so unequal lengths drift against the song.

Example: a three-step channel at Clock Mod /9 plays a note every 1.5 seconds, so its three notes 60, 62, 64 cycle every 4.5 seconds. The slot repeats every 64 steps (10.7 seconds), which is not a whole number of cycles. With Off, the cycle carries on across the boundary, so the third note, 64, sounds at 12 seconds. With On, note 60 sounds exactly at the boundary. With Song mode Off the slot is not repeated by the song, so the reset does not apply.

recipes.title: Restart a slow channel on each repeat

title: Parameter Slides Wrap
summary: Let the final parameter slide of a loop run to the first lock across the loop boundary. Default: Off.
prose:
Wrap param slides is Off by default. A parameter slide moves a value smoothly from one lock to the next. The last lock in a loop has no later lock to slide toward, so with Off it holds its value and the first lock is recalled when the loop restarts. With On, and the current song pattern repeating, the last slide runs on to the first lock of the same pattern, so the value arrives at the first lock with the first note of the next loop.

Example: CC 1 locks of 24 on step 1, 96 on step 3 and 48 on step 4, with a slide on step 4 in a four-step loop at 90 BPM. With Off, CC 1 holds 48 through step 4 and jumps to 24 at the loop point. With On, it descends in a straight line from 48 to 24 over one sixteenth-note step (one sixth of a second) and reaches 24 with the next first note.

details.title: What counts as the boundary
details.text: Wrapping follows the channel's configured start and end steps, so with a four-step range the wrap happens at step 4, not at step 64. It is also limited by the song pattern's global length.

details.title: What it does not join
details.text: Slides do not run from one song pattern to a different one; the wrap happens only inside a repeating pattern.

recipes.title: Sweep a filter around the loop

title: Elektron Program Changes
summary: Send program changes for Mosaic song-pattern selections and transitions. Default: Off.
prose:
Elektron program changes is Off by default. With On, Mosaic sends a MIDI program change whenever it selects or moves to a song slot, so a receiving pattern-based instrument follows your song. The example in this manual uses the Digitakt device configuration; any receiver that accepts program changes on the same channel works the same way.

The value counts from 0 on the wire. Song slot 1 sends value 0, which the receiver labels pattern 1; slot 2 sends 1, labelled pattern 2. While playing, each incoming slot is announced once, at least half a step (about 83 ms at 90 BPM) before its first note, and pressing Play first sends the slot that is about to sound. Set the receiver to accept program changes, and set the channel in Elektron p.change channel.

recipes.title: Follow Mosaic's slots with a Digitakt

title: Elektron Program Change Channel
summary: Set the MIDI channel for Elektron program changes. Range: 1–16. Default: 10.
prose: Elektron p.change channel sets the MIDI channel Mosaic uses for program changes, 1–16. The default is 10, the channel most Elektron devices listen on out of the box. Change it only if your receiver is set to a different channel. The same channel must be set on the receiver and in Mosaic, or the receiver ignores the messages.

recipes.title: Send program changes on channel 1

title: Parameter Lock Options
summary: Set lock lead time, trigless locks and resending of unchanged lock values.
prose: Open PARAMS > MOSAIC > Parameter locks. This group holds Lock lead time (how early a lock is sent before its step), Trigless locks (whether locks on steps without a trig are sent) and the option for resending unchanged lock values. Resend unchanged locks is On by default; with Off, Mosaic sends a slot's value only when it changes, which eases the load on busy projects. Turn E2 to a row and E3 to change it.

details.title: Choose the comparison you need
details.text: Use Lock lead time to compare the same CC value arriving with its note or just before it. Use Trigless locks to compare whether CC 1 = 72 is sent on a removed third trig. Use Param Slides for the separate 24-to-96 ramp; slides are edited on Trig params rather than in this options group.

title: Trigless Locks
summary: Apply parameter locks on steps without an active trig. Default: On.
prose:
Trigless locks is On by default. A trigless lock is a parameter lock on a step with no trig, a rest. With On, Mosaic still sends the lock on that step, so a filter or other control keeps moving while no note plays. With Off, locks on steps without a trig are skipped, and only steps that have a trig send their locks.

A trig that fails its probability check still counts as a trig, so its locks are sent either way; only a removed trig is affected by this option. Example: CC 1 locks of 24, 48, 72 and 96 on steps 1–4. Remove the trig on step 3. With Off, CC 1 sends 24, 48 and 96. With On, it sends all four, 72 included. Locks are sent just before the step's note.

recipes.title: Hear automation on rests

title: Quantiser Options
summary: Set note-mask quantisation, channel scale-lock lifetime and pentatonic restrictions.
prose: Open PARAMS > MOSAIC > Quantiser. This group holds the note-mask options (Snap note masks to scale and Quantise note masks), Scales lock until ptn end, and the three pentatonic restrictions (Lock all to pent., Lock random to pent. and Lock merged to pent.). The pentatonic options use a five-note selection per scale, listed under Lock merged to pentatonic.

title: Snap Note Masks to Scale
summary: Snap note masks to the selected scale without degree or rotation changes. Default: On.
prose: Snap note masks to scale defaults to On. On snaps note masks to the selected scale. Scale-degree and rotation adjustments do not alter these snapped masks.

title: Quantise Note Masks
summary: Fully quantise note masks, including scale-degree and transposition changes. Default: Off.
prose: Quantise note masks defaults to Off. On fully quantises all note masks to the selected scale and applies scale-degree and transposition adjustments. This setting overrides Snap note masks to scale.

title: Scales Lock Until Pattern End
summary: Retain channel scale locks until channel wrap or replacement. Default: On.
prose:
Scales lock until ptn end defaults to On and controls channel scale locks.

On retains a channel lock until the channel wraps to its start or another channel scale lock replaces it.

Off clears the previous lock at the next active trig that passes its probability check. A probability-rejected trig does not clear it. A new scale lock on the accepted trig applies normally.

Global scale-track locks are independent of this option. They remain until replacement or global-track wrap.

title: Lock All to Pentatonic
summary: Restrict resolved notes to Mosaic’s five-note selection for the selected scale. Default: Off.
prose:
Lock all to pent. is Off by default. With On, every resolved note is restricted to Mosaic's five-note selection for the selected scale: degrees 1/2/3/5/6 for Major, 1/3/4/5/7 for Minor, 2/3/5/6/7 for Lydian, and so on (the full list is under Lock merged to pentatonic). A note outside the selection moves to the nearest allowed pitch, and an exact tie picks the lower one.

Example in C major with a seven-step pattern of degrees I–VII: Off plays 60, 62, 64, 65, 67, 69, 71. On plays 60, 62, 64, 64, 67, 69, 72 (F falls to E, B rises to C). In C natural minor, On plays 60, 63, 63, 65, 67, 67, 70. In Lydian, the tonic C snaps down to B, giving 59, 62, 64, 67, 67, 69, 71.

recipes.title: Hear every note restricted

title: Lock Random to Pentatonic
summary: Restrict notes changed by random trig locks to Mosaic’s five-note scale selection. Default: On.
prose:
Lock random to pent. is On by default. Random Note and Twos Random Note shift a note by a random number of scale degrees. With On, a note moved by a nonzero random offset snaps to the nearest note of Mosaic's five-note selection for the scale; with Off it lands on any of the seven scale degrees. A step whose random offset is zero keeps its own note.

Example with Random Note 4 (offsets -2 to +2 degrees) on C D E F: with Off the draws can land on F (65) and B (59) as well as C, D, E, G and A. With On, every note moved by a random offset is one of C D E G A. The capture uses a fixed random seed; your own runs will differ each time.

recipes.title: Compare random notes with and without the filter

title: Lock Merged to Pentatonic
summary: Restrict merged notes to Mosaic’s scale-specific five-note selection. Default: On.
prose:
Lock merged to pent. is On by default. A merge mode combines the notes of several patterns; this option restricts the result to Mosaic's five-note selection for the selected scale. Example in C major with pattern 1 on degrees I, III, V, VII and pattern 2 on III, V, VII, I: Average merge gives degrees II, IV, VI, IV. With Off you hear 62, 65, 69, 65 (D F A F). With On, F is not in the major selection and snaps to the nearer E, so you hear 62, 64, 69, 64.

The selections use one-based degrees of each named seven-note scale:
- Major and Harmonic Major: 1/2/3/5/6.
- Minor, Harmonic Minor and Melodic Minor: 1/3/4/5/7.
- Dorian: 1/2/4/5/7.
- Phrygian: 1/3/4/6/7.
- Lydian: 2/3/5/6/7.
- Mixolydian: 1/2/4/5/6.
- Locrian: 2/3/4/6/7.

Apply the named scale's alterations to these degrees. The selection does not always retain the tonic or avoid semitones.

Merged values remain seven-note scale degrees, not five-note indices. Their scale pitches snap to the nearest selected pitch across repeated octaves. An exact tie selects the lower pitch. Snapping can cross an octave boundary.

For example, Lydian C snaps to the B below it. Melodic Minor A snaps down to G rather than the equally distant B.

The scale root is used when set; otherwise, the song root is used. The effective octave offset is applied afterward.

recipes.title: Compare merged notes with and without the filter

title: MIDI Controller Options
summary: Set MIDI keyboard white-key mapping and scale transformations.
prose: Open PARAMS > MOSAIC > Midi control. It holds Map scale to white keys and the three Honour switches (degree, rotations, transpose). They change what a MIDI keyboard plays and records on the selected channel: with mapping Off the keyboard plays its own notes, and with mapping On the white keys play the selected scale, optionally shaped by the Scale Editor's degree, rotation and transposition.

details.title: Evidence: keyboard output scope
details.text: The enabled keyboard phrase is complete. The earlier startup output is truncated and is not the acceptance target; compare the dedicated option-enabled playback window. Each reference example begins with its own stated Degree, Rotation and Transpose settings.

recipes.title: Map an external keyboard through the scale’s rotated degrees
Apply scale rotation and global transpose to every keyboard key

title: Map Scale to White Keys
summary: Map the selected scale onto MIDI keyboard white keys, starting at C. Default: Off.
prose: Map scale to white keys is Off by default, so the keyboard plays its own notes. With On, the selected scale is laid out on the white keys, with the scale's first note on C: in C major the white keys C D E F G A B C play 60, 62, 64, 65, 67, 69, 71, 72. Choose a different scale and the white keys follow it: in C natural minor they play 60, 62, 63, 65, 67, 68, 70, 72. Black keys are outside this lesson.

details.title: White-key workflow scope
details.text: This procedure covers white-key scale mapping. Black-key mapping is outside this example.

recipes.title: Play a minor scale on the white keys

title: Honor Scale Rotations
summary: Apply scale rotation to mapped MIDI keyboard input. Default: Off.
prose:
Honour scale rotations is Off by default. With On, the scale's rotation setting from the Scale Editor also applies to the white-key mapping. Rotation 2 lowers the last two scale positions, the white keys A and B, by an octave. In natural minor with degree II also honoured, C to C plays 62, 63, 65, 67, 68, 58, 60, 74.

Honour switches only change the white-key mapping. Set them after turning on Map scale to white keys; with it Off the keyboard plays its original notes.

details.title: Mapping dependency
details.text: These honour switches affect the quantised white-key mapping. With Map scale to white keys Off, MIDI input uses the original incoming pitch.

details.title: Evidence: keyboard output scope
details.text: The enabled keyboard phrase is complete. The earlier startup output is truncated and is not the acceptance target; compare the dedicated option-enabled playback window. Each reference example begins with its own stated Degree, Rotation and Transpose settings.

recipes.title: Map an external keyboard through the scale’s rotated degrees

title: Honor Scale Degree
summary: Apply scale degree to mapped MIDI keyboard input. Default: Off.
prose:
Honour scale degree is Off by default. With On, the scale's degree setting from the Scale Editor starts the white-key mapping on that degree. With degree II in natural minor, white key C plays the scale's second note: C to C plays 62, 63, 65, 67, 68, 70, 72, 74, against 60, 62, 63, 65, 67, 68, 70, 72 with the switch Off.

Honour switches only change the white-key mapping. Set them after turning on Map scale to white keys; with it Off the keyboard plays its original notes.

details.title: Mapping dependency
details.text: These honour switches affect the quantised white-key mapping. With Map scale to white keys Off, MIDI input uses the original incoming pitch.

title: Honour Scale Transpose
summary: Apply scale transposition to mapped MIDI keyboard input. Default: Off.
prose:
Honour scale transpose is Off by default. With On, the scale's transposition from the Scale Editor also shifts the white-key mapping. With degree II, rotation 2 and transpose +2 all honoured, C to C in natural minor plays 64, 65, 67, 69, 70, 60, 62, 76; with only transpose honoured, every note is two semitones above the plain mapping.

Honour switches only change the white-key mapping. Set them after turning on Map scale to white keys; with it Off the keyboard plays its original notes.

details.title: Mapping dependency
details.text: These honour switches affect the quantised white-key mapping. With Map scale to white keys Off, MIDI input uses the original incoming pitch.

details.title: Evidence: keyboard output scope
details.text: The enabled keyboard phrase is complete. The earlier startup output is truncated and is not the acceptance target; compare the dedicated option-enabled playback window. Each reference example begins with its own stated Degree, Rotation and Transpose settings.

recipes.title: Apply scale rotation and global transpose to every keyboard key

title: Screen Options
summary: Set decorative screen motion.
prose: Open PARAMS > MOSAIC > Screen. It holds UI motion, which turns the decorative screen animation on or off. Nothing in this group changes sequencer timing, input or output.

title: UI Motion
summary: Enable decorative screen motion. Default: On. This setting does not change sequencer timing or input.
prose:
UI motion is On by default. It controls the decorative animation of the norns screen only; it never changes sequencer timing, input or the notes you hear. With Off the screen is still.

With On, a miniature graphic in the header identifies the screen and moves with the music: while playing it follows the sequencer's transport pulses, while stopped it follows the selected norns musical clock without starting playback. With Off, or if the clock is missing or invalid, it holds its rest pose. The start-up animation, the shadow that glides across the Masks and Trig params grids, values that roll into place, the characters on some screens and the small dial beside a single numeric value are decoration and are governed by the same setting.

Only the selected label or value that is too long for its row scrolls right to left. Fitting labels, neighbouring rows, the title and controls stay still. A long selected value first gets its own full-width row. With motion Off, shortened text ends in ~, and an exact value that cannot fit shows LAYOUT OVERFLOW instead of silently changing.

The light running round the Mosaic mark, the shadow gliding across the Masks and Trig params grids (diagonally when it changes row) and values rolling into place all stop with motion Off. The Rhythm Doctor dances to the tempo of the captured bank, and the Merge Shape garden sways and the Harmony choir bobs while the sequencer plays. Motion never delays input and never hides a value for more than a moment.

details.title: Selected overflow text
details.text: Overflow scrolling is restricted to the selected label or value. Fitting text and neighboring rows remain stationary. Off stops scrolling; ~ indicates shortened text, and exact values that cannot fit report LAYOUT OVERFLOW.

details.title: Miniature header timing
details.text: Playing uses musical sequencer transport position. Stopped uses the selected musical clock and does not start Mosaic or sound notes. Off or missing/invalid clock holds the rest pose. Native PARAMS owns its own screen.

recipes.title: Compare the screen with motion Off and On

title: Sinfonion Connect
summary: Synchronise Mosaic with Sinfonion using the external norns2sinfonion bridge.
prose: Mosaic can synchronise harmony with a Eurorack Sinfonion module through the DIY [norns2sinfonion](https://github.com/subvertnormality/norns2sinfonion) bridge. This needs extra hardware and software: follow the bridge's own setup instructions, then use Mosaic as usual. Mosaic has no separate Sinfonion option in PARAMS > MOSAIC.

title: LFOs and Modulation
summary: Matrix routes toolkit modulation sources to device parameters.
prose:
Mosaic supports Matrix mod and toolkit. Matrix routes modulation sources to device parameters; toolkit supplies LFOs and other rhythmic modulators.

Install and configure the mods using their documentation:
- [Matrix](https://github.com/sixolet/matrix)
- [Toolkit](https://github.com/sixolet/toolkit)


Start with [Make a small CC move with Macro 1](#lfos-and-modulation/matrix-macro-modest-cc), the complete recorded example: set depth 0.10, move CC 1 from 32 to 38 and back to 32 while the same phrase plays, then return Macro 1 to zero.


Advanced: [Set up a clocked LFO at full depth](#lfos-and-modulation/lesson/toolkit-clocked-lfo-menu-clock) starts from lfo 1 at depth 1.00 and changes the LFO clock.

details.title: Installed mods
details.text: Matrix provides routing. Toolkit provides modulation sources. Their installed versions determine the native menu sequence. This feature has no additional Mosaic grid shortcut.

details.title: Step-lock precedence
details.text: Modulation can add or subtract from an outgoing MIDI CC value. Clearing the modulation restores the value supplied by its default or step lock.

title: Musical Merge and Voice Leading
summary: Foundation and Fragments reshape merged output without rewriting patterns. Harmony places output voices; its default is Off.
prose:
Merge Shape changes a channel’s merged rhythm. Harmony places output notes in specified registers. Neither feature rewrites source patterns. Older projects restore their saved Skip, Only or All Strategy and retain its original MIDI, timing and random behavior. Foundation and Fragments are other exclusive choices of the same Strategy selector.

Merge modes, Merge Shape and Harmony are consecutive Channel tasks. Merge Shape and Voice leading use vertical lists. Editable rows display their current value. Submenus display OPEN >. The selected row is marked >.

1. Open Merge Shape or Harmony from Channel tasks.
2. Turn E2 to select a row.
3. Turn E3 to change a staged value.
4. Press K3 on OPEN > to open that settings list. The bottom line names the action, for example K3 OPEN RHYTHM.
5. Press K3 on an ordinary value row to validate and apply the complete draft.

Action rows, including Create group, Four-part smooth, Delete group and Reset map, display a plain >. Delete group and Reset map require confirmation.

Press K2 to discard a dirty draft, or to return from an opened list to its parent. Turn E1 to return to the feature’s first screen and discard an unapplied draft. From the first screen, E1 returns to Channel tasks.

A stopped edit applies immediately. During playback, Merge Shape displays NEXT CYCLE and applies before the next channel-cycle onset. Harmony displays NEXT PATTERN and applies at the next global pattern boundary. Stop activates the latest applied request for the next start.

Merge Shape shows a read-only Strategy summary. Its Strategy selector action discards an unapplied parameter draft and opens the shared selector on Merge modes. Grid (14,8) selects the same Skip, Only, All, Foundation and Fragments choices. A strategy request is immediate; parameter drafts still need K3 Apply. Active is sounding output, while Pending is an accepted request awaiting its displayed boundary.

details.title: Applying changes
details.text: Stopped edits apply immediately. During playback, Merge Shape normally displays NEXT CYCLE and applies at the next channel-cycle onset. Harmony displays NEXT PATTERN and applies at the next global pattern boundary. A shared group-reference change can also queue Merge Shape for NEXT PATTERN. Stop settles the latest applied request.

details.title: Source patterns
details.text: E3 edits a draft until K3 applies it. Grid editing can cancel a dirty draft. Merge Shape and Harmony change channel output; they do not rewrite source patterns.

title: Merge Shape
summary: Foundation keeps one anchor pattern’s trigs and adds a repeatable selection of trigs from the other assigned patterns; Phrase changes how many additions play from loop to loop.
prose:
Merge Shape turns several assigned patterns into one channel part. The Anchor pattern’s trigs always play. Trigs from the other assigned patterns are additions: Merge Shape decides how many of them play, how loud, and how close to an anchor. The source patterns are never changed.

Terms used on this page: Anchor is the pattern whose trigs are protected. An addition is a trig from another assigned pattern that Foundation admits. A draft is a set of edits shown on screen but not yet applied; K3 applies it and K2 discards it. Active is the strategy that is sounding, and Pending is a request waiting for its boundary.

[Captured two-cycle Build workflow](#merge-shape/foundation-two-cycle-build)

[Captured Foundation settings and output](#merge-shape/foundation-protected-and-added)

Choose Foundation with the shared Strategy selector on grid (14,8) or Merge modes. Merge Shape shows Strategy as a read-only summary; its Strategy selector action opens Merge modes and discards an unapplied parameter draft. K2 returns with the accepted configuration loaded. Foundation controls trigs only; note, velocity and length merge settings remain active. Choose Skip, Only or All to restore legacy trig merging with retained values. Foundation selects
one assigned pattern as the protected Anchor. Other assigned trig patterns offer
candidate additions at non-anchor steps; overlaps remain one anchor. Amount
admits a deterministic, seed-ranked subset, Accent scales addition velocity, and
Gap suppresses additions within 0–8 circular channel steps of an anchor. Anchor
velocity remains authored. Explicit channel/step masks still win, probability
can still reject an onset, and source patterns are never flattened or changed.

Phrase Cycles can be 1, 2, 4 or 8. Flat, Build, Answer and Fill are stored as
visible per-cycle percentages; changing a percentage makes a Custom curve.
Fixed repeats the same ranked additions. Per phrase changes ranking only after a
complete phrase. Each channel loop advances its own CYCLE counter—even with
polymetric ranges, swing or mute—and Stop restarts at cycle 1.

Keep anchor pitch uses the anchor pattern's relative note on anchor steps before
normal scale conversion. Addition Target can be Legacy, the full effective
scale, selected effective degree indices, or the immutable material of an enabled
Harmony Ensemble group. Targets affect admitted additions only. Note masks,
random shifts and fixed-note operations keep their existing precedence and show
a bypass rather than being quantised twice. Nearest-note ties choose the lower
pitch. A missing/empty target visibly falls back to the legacy pitch.

Foundation ranking is repeatable for the saved seed and grows as a nested set:
raising Amount cannot remove an already selected addition while source, gap,
seed and phrase are unchanged.

Fragments is another shared Strategy choice. Foundation's Interlock and Structure settings remain staged parameter edits: K3 applies the draft, K2 discards it. During playback the shown boundary is NEXT CYCLE, or NEXT PATTERN when applicable. Strategy choices themselves request immediately and do not need K3 Apply.

details.title: Anchor and precedence
details.text: Foundation retains anchor velocity. Note, velocity and length merge settings still apply. Explicit masks take precedence. Probability can reject an onset. Source patterns are unchanged.

details.title: Saved trig merge while Foundation is active
details.text: While Foundation is Active, Merge modes shows Active FOUNDATION and Foundation decides the channel's trigs. Your saved Skip, Only or All trig merge setting is kept and is not edited. Choose Skip, Only or All on the Strategy selector to restore it. Note, velocity and length merge rows stay editable.

details.title: Undo
details.text: Applying a Merge Shape draft, including the Interlock and Structure edits made in the same draft, is one step in the channel's Memory. Open History in Channel tasks and turn E3 back one step to restore the previous configuration.

details.title: Amount and variation
details.text: For unchanged source, Gap, Seed and phrase, increasing Amount retains previously admitted additions. Fixed repeats the ranking. Per phrase changes the ranking after a complete phrase.

details.title: Amount, Accent and Phrase do different jobs
details.text: Add amount and the Phrase curve decide how many additions play. Add accent decides how loud they are. Lowering Add accent therefore makes additions quieter without removing any; it does not change the Phrase curve.

title: Fragments
summary: Fragments cuts the channel loop into 4-, 8- or 16-step sections and plays each section from one assigned pattern, chosen by a repeatable seed.
prose:
[Captured Fragments seed and playback workflow](#fragments/fragments-seed-source-choice)

Fragments is a separate mode for building a phrase from pieces of the assigned
patterns. Choose Fragments with the shared Strategy selector, then open Rhythm from Merge Shape for Size (4,
8 or 16 steps), Keep anchor, Anchor (shown only with Keep anchor) and Seed. The
channel loop is cut into fragments of Size steps counted from the channel's own
start step; the last fragment is shorter when the loop does not divide evenly,
and a loop shorter than Size is one fragment. Fragments never cross the loop end.

Each fragment plays one assigned pattern, chosen repeatably by the Seed: the
same seed always gives the same choice. The fragment keeps that pattern's own
trigs, notes, velocities and lengths exactly, so the legacy trig, note,
velocity and length merge modes and merged-pentatonic do not apply while
Fragments is active. Merge modes marks its retained note, velocity and length rows inactive, with values such as `AVERAGE SAVED`. These rows and their grid buttons do not edit saved values. Choose Skip, Only or All to restore the retained settings. A note longer than the gap to
the next onset on the loop is shortened to that gap. Keep anchor also plays the
Anchor pattern's trigs where the fragment's own pattern has none; where both have
a trig, the fragment's pattern wins. With no assigned pattern the mode falls back
to legacy merging and Result says `ASSIGN PATTERN`.

Phrase shows only Cycles and Variation in this mode. Fixed repeats the same
fragment sources every phrase; Per phrase draws new ones for each phrase.
Shape percentages, Amount, Accent and Gap do not apply. Fragments hides Pitch; choose the adjacent Harmony task directly for voice leading. Explicit masks still win and probability can still reject an
onset. The channel grid shows exactly the trigs the fragments play.

details.title: Loop boundaries
details.text: Fragments start at the channel loop’s start step. The last fragment is shorter when the loop does not divide evenly. A loop shorter than Size is one fragment. Fragments do not cross the loop end.

details.title: Overrides and fallback
details.text: Legacy trig, note, velocity and length merges and merged-pentatonic do not apply in Fragments. Explicit masks and probability still apply. With no assigned pattern, Result displays ASSIGN PATTERN and uses legacy merging.

recipes.title: Set four-step fragments

title: Interlock
summary: Interlock removes a follower channel’s Foundation additions that fall within 0 to 4 steps of a leader channel’s anchors.
prose:
[Captured Interlock Leader and Window workflow](#interlock/interlock-leader-window)

Interlock makes one channel's Foundation additions leave room for another
channel's anchors. On the follower's Rhythm screen, Interlock opens Leader (Off
or any other channel) and Window (0–4 of the follower's steps). An addition is
removed when a leader anchor falls within Window steps of it; Window 0 removes
only additions that start exactly with a leader anchor. Anchors of either channel
are never removed, so an addition removed here simply does not play.

Leader anchors are the anchor pattern's trigs in the leader's loop, planned from
the song, not what the leader happened to sound: probability, mute and swing do
not change them, and swing or shuffle never change which additions are removed.
Channels at different clock divisions or loop lengths are compared in musical
time from Start. The leader must itself use Foundation for its anchors to count;
otherwise Status says `LEADER OFF` or `LEADER MISSING` and nothing is removed.

A channel can follow one leader, and a channel that has a leader cannot be one:
Apply refuses a chain with `LEADER HAS LEADER` or `CHANNEL IS A LEADER` and
keeps your draft. Where Mosaic cannot plan the leader exactly—after a clock
division, loop range or song change while playing (`RESYNC`, until the next
Start or song realign) or beyond its planning budget (`PLAN LIMIT`)—the
follower plays all of its admitted additions for that loop and shows why.
Status on the Interlock screen and the Interlock row on Result show `ON` or the
bypass.

Interlock plans additions when a follower wraps its loop. Many followers wrapping together increase the work on that step. If you use many followers, stagger their loop lengths or wrap points.

details.title: Leader anchors
details.text: Mute, probability and swing do not change the nominal leader-anchor decision. Window 0 removes only additions that start exactly with a leader anchor. Interlock compares where leader anchors start, not how long the leader’s note lasts, so it does not keep space free for a sustained leader note.

details.title: Bypass status
details.text: LEADER OFF, LEADER MISSING, RESYNC and PLAN LIMIT identify inactive filtering. During a planning bypass, admitted additions play. Gap and Amount still apply.

recipes.title: Set Window 0

title: Structure
summary: Structure moves selected Foundation notes to the nearest pitch class of an enabled Harmony group’s chord.
prose:
[Captured Structure group and marker workflow](#structure/structure-anchor-chord-and-delete)

Structure snaps chosen moments of a Foundation line to a chord while the notes
in between keep their own pitch. Pitch opens Structure: Markers (Off, Anchors,
Every 4 or Every 8) and Chord group, an enabled Harmony Ensemble group. Anchors
marks every anchor onset; Every 4 and Every 8 mark steps 1, 5, 9… or 1, 9… of the
channel loop counted from its start step. A note at a marker is converted to the
scale as usual and then moved to the nearest pitch class of the group's chord,
taking the lower one on a tie. Notes between markers keep their Addition Target
(additions) or their own pitch (anchors); Mosaic makes no claim that they
resolve. Note masks, random shifts and fixed notes still win at a marker.

Apply needs an enabled group while Markers is on. If the group becomes
unavailable during playback the markers play their ordinary pitch and Result
says `CHORD MISSING`. Deleting or disabling the group turns Markers Off for every
channel that uses it in the same change; Delete group lists those channels first.
During playback that change waits for the next pattern boundary, and a Merge
Shape edit applied to one of those channels before then waits with it and shows
`NEXT PATTERN` instead of `NEXT CYCLE`.
A snapped marker keeps its chord tone when Harmony Revoice or Ensemble would move
it: Harmony's Result says `MARKER PRIORITY`. With Harmony Pattern, a mapped note
value that snaps to a different pitch class at a marker than it plays between
markers has no single mapped pitch, so it is silent at both, whichever fallback
is chosen; unmapped values keep their own pitch.

details.title: Markers and pitch precedence
details.text: Markers count from the channel loop’s start step. The nearest chord pitch class is selected; ties select the lower pitch. Note masks, random shifts and fixed notes retain their precedence.

details.title: Group deletion and disable
details.text: Deleting or disabling a referenced group turns affected Markers Off in the same transaction. During playback, that change waits for NEXT PATTERN. Pending linked Merge Shape edits wait for the same boundary.

title: Result and Reason
summary: Result shows what a step is and why. Reason lists, in order, the decisions that excluded an addition.
prose:
Use Result and Reason when an expected addition is silent. They tell you whether the step is an anchor, an admitted addition or empty, and which rule removed it, so you can fix the setting instead of editing a pattern or adding a mask.

The examples below use a follower channel with Foundation (anchor Pattern 1 on steps 1 to 4, additions from Pattern 2 on steps 5 and 7) that follows channel 2 through Interlock, where channel 2 has an anchor on step 5. See Interlock to set that up.

1. Turn E1 for Channel tasks, select Merge Shape with E2 and press K3. Select Result and press K3.
2. Select Step with E2. Turn E3 to the step to inspect. Role and Decision show that step.
3. Select Reason with E2 and press K3. The Merge Reason dashboard opens with six rows. K2 returns to Result.

The six rows of Reason:

- Step: the step you are inspecting.
- Role: what the step is, followed by its source patterns. ANCHOR is a trig from the anchor pattern, ADDITION P2 is an addition taken from Pattern 2, and EMPTY means nothing plays.
- Decision: OK when the step plays, otherwise every rule that excluded it, in order. GAP comes first, then INTERLOCK CH02. When both apply, both are listed, as in GAP, INTERLOCK.
- Interlock: ON while the leader’s anchors are being avoided, OFF when there is no leader, RESYNC or PLAN LIMIT when Interlock cannot plan the leader and is bypassed.
- Velocity: the velocity the step plays, or NONE when it does not play.
- Pitch target: LEGACY unless an Addition Target or Structure marker applies.

A suppressed addition shows Role EMPTY with its source patterns, for example EMPTY P2, and Velocity NONE. EMPTY P2 does not mean Pattern 2 has no trig on that step. Read Decision to see why the candidate was removed.

During a planning bypass, Gap and Amount still decide the step as if Interlock were Off.

A fragment step names its fragment and source, for example FRAGMENT 1 P03 or KEPT ANCHOR. A Structure marker shows MARKER CHORD G01 when its pitch is snapped, CHORD MISSING when the group is unavailable, or a reason such as BYPASS NOTE MASK, BYPASS RANDOM, BYPASS FIXED or BYPASS QUANTISED FIXED.

When a leader is set, Result also shows the Interlock status. A queued edit refused at the loop boundary is shown as Rejected. Silence-aware Interlock, which would keep space free while another channel’s notes sustain, is not available in this release.

details.title: Combined reasons
details.text: Reason can display GAP and INTERLOCK together, with GAP first. The Interlock row is separate and shows ON, OFF, RESYNC or PLAN LIMIT. A planning bypass does not remove Gap or Amount decisions.

details.title: Pitch status
details.text: MARKER CHORD G01 identifies a snapped marker. BYPASS NOTE MASK, BYPASS RANDOM and fixed-note bypasses identify retained pitches. CHORD MISSING identifies the ordinary-pitch fallback.

details.title: Suppressed addition readout
details.text: A suppressed Foundation addition shows Role EMPTY with its source patterns, and Velocity NONE. Decision tells you whether a candidate was excluded or the source step was empty.

title: Harmony
summary: Harmony provides Off, Revoice, Pattern and Ensemble modes for channel output pitch placement.
prose:
Harmony changes the pitch a channel sends, not its rhythm. Open it from Channel tasks (Voice leading list: Mode, Group, Preset, Tone Map in Pattern mode, Register, Bass, Groups, Rules, Entry, Result). Tone Map is the page that maps written notes to voices. Register sets each voice’s range. Entry holds the Failure fallback. Result shows what was planned and sent.

[Captured Harmony range failure and fallback](#harmony/harmony-range-failure-and-fallback)

[Captured Harmony Revoice workflow](#harmony/harmony-revoice-two-voices)

Harmony offers four mutually exclusive channel modes:

- Off follows the ordinary Mosaic pitch path exactly.
- Revoice takes the actual root and enabled chord-mask voices after Mosaic's
  pitch-class decisions, preserving their pitch classes and sounding count while
  choosing legal octaves and assignments.
- Pattern maps explicit effective relative values in the current merge binding
  to Bass, Inner1–3 or Top. Repeated mapped values reuse one pitch for the entire
  harmonic frame; unmapped values remain Raw. Random, fixed, absolute-mask and
  chord-mask events visibly bypass Pattern. Conflicting aliases fail closed.
- Ensemble assigns Bass/Inner/Top roles to one to five explicit monophonic
  channels. Each member retains its own rhythm, velocity, gate, clock and route,
  but its pitch is replaced by the shared frame. A conflicting local scale lock
  temporarily uses the ordinary pitch path (`LOCAL SCALE BYPASS`); a channel or
  step octave override does the same (`LOCAL OCTAVE BYPASS`).

Register rows set inclusive MIDI Low/High, Centre and Preferred leap for every
role. Smooth prioritises literal common tones and economical movement; Compact
prioritises register centre/spacing; Independent prioritises movement without a
common-tone score. Hard options cover crossing, exact unison, strict leap and
strict bass direction. Bass can be Root, an explicit Inversion tone, Smooth or
an exact Pedal. Revoice pedals must already be in its input material; only an
Ensemble group can explicitly allow a non-chord pedal.

The deterministic solver searches every legal pitch-class placement inside the
configured ranges (up to five voices) and never clamps an illegal result. A frame
with no solution silences affected mapped voices by default; Legacy fallback is
explicit. A bounded search reports `BUDGET EXCEEDED` rather than emitting a
partial answer. Preparing a frame does not change voice history: the first real
scheduled onset consumes it, while redraws, rests, failed probability, mute and
missing output do not. Delayed strums and arpeggios keep the pitch snapshot made
at their onset, and Note Off always releases the pitch and route actually sent.

[Captured NO VOICING and Legacy fallback](#harmony/harmony-range-failure-and-fallback)

The Channel grid remains the chronological trig/mask surface. Foundation anchors
and additions therefore appear as active steps there. After a step plays, the
Pattern Note grid moves that step's bright note LED to the final effective pitch
that the native 21-position note range can represent. Switch its upper, centred
or lower seven-note bank as usual to inspect octave placement. Raw and bypassed
events use the ordinary pre-Harmony position; turning Harmony Off restores the
ordinary merged/scale positions immediately. An exact pitch outside that native
range has no false in-range LED and remains available in Result/Note Dashboard.

This display is read-only: touching the projected Note fader still edits its
selected source-pattern value. Until the changed step plays again, the edited
source is displayed rather than a stale output. Final Harmony pitches are also
shown on Output (its Pitch and Sent rows) and on Harmony's Result screen, one row
per voice as the planned and sent note (`C3 > C3`). Result uses its Step row to
select one coherent event chain; on Note
Dashboard, holding a grid step temporarily inspects that step instead of combining
it with a later delayed event. A step with no recorded event says `NO EVENT` and
shows no planned or emitted pitch; it never borrows the latest event from another
step. This readout occupies the bottom two lines of the Note Dashboard, which is
the row tooltips use, so while a harmony event is being shown there the page
clears that row and tooltips are not visible on it. Result status names local scale/octave bypasses, explicit Legacy fallback
and the specific no-voicing reason. For an Ensemble group, any member bypass or failure is
surfaced even when another member has a valid voicing. The projection never writes
back into a shared pattern. Copy/save stores
versioned configuration, not running solver or phrase history. Missing optional
configuration loads as Off; unknown schema versions reject the project before it
replaces the active project.

details.title: Shared channel, Song and grid controls
details.text: Select a channel at (3,8), choose its row-1 channel number and open Channel tasks through E1. Use E2 to choose Device, Masks, Clock, Trig params or Harmony and K3 to open the page. On Device, E2 selects a row, E3 changes the named sound and K3 applies it. On Masks, E2 selects Note, Vel, Len or Chd1/Chd2 and E3 changes the value; hold a step while turning E3 for a local exception. Add a trig mask by holding K1, tapping the step and releasing K1. Steps 1–16 use grid row 4, 17–32 row 5, 33–48 row 6 and 49–64 row 7; each group begins at column 1. Hold the first step and tap the last to set a channel range. For Song slots, press Song at (6,8); slots 1–3 are (1,1)–(3,1). Hold the source slot, tap the destination, release, then tap the destination to edit it. The length fader sets 13 steps at (3,7), 16 after three taps at (8,7), 32 at (4,7) and 64 at (7,7). In Song Tempo and feel, choose Tempo and set 90 with E3; set each channel Rate /1 on Clock and apply with K3. In Trig params, E2 selects a slot, K2 opens its assignment list, E3 highlights a parameter, K3 assigns it and K2 returns. Hold a step and turn E3 to set its lock; K2 clears a held-step lock.

title: Performance Management
summary: Channel count, clock rates, parameter slides, trigless locks and n.b. devices affect sequencer workload.
prose:
Channel count, clock rate, trig locks, parameter slides and n.b. devices affect Mosaic’s workload. Heavy workload can delay sequencing and make external clock synchronization unreliable.

- Use greater care with high clock rates, trig locks, parameter slides and n.b. devices as channel count increases.
- High clock rates and multipliers increase sequencer workload.
- Use global parameter slides sparingly. Use step parameter slides when global sliding is unnecessary, and limit the total number of slides.
- Disable trigless locks when the additional modulation granularity is not needed.
- Limit the number of n.b. devices.

A test on version 1.1.1 found unreliable external synchronization with one Doubledecker n.b. device at 110 BPM, trigless parameters, locks on most steps for all 10 trig parameters across four channels, and 40 parameters using global parameter sliding. Other combinations can produce different results. This earlier example does not specify a universal limit for the current version.

details.title: Earlier timing test
details.text: The 110 BPM Doubledecker example comes from testing on version 1.1.1. It is not a universal current limit. Host and emulator timing do not establish physical norns scheduling accuracy.

details.title: Reducing workload
details.text: Use step slides where a global slide is unnecessary. Disable trigless locks when their additional modulation detail is not needed. Compare changes using the same arrangement and clock source.

title: Development
summary: Run the repository tests on a development machine before opening a pull request.
prose:
This section is for people changing Mosaic's code, not for playing it. Before opening a pull request, run the repository tests on a development machine:

```
./test.sh
```

Do not run the harness on norns. It downloads a copy of the norns repository, which can conflict with the device's own installation. If you ran it on the device by mistake, delete /code/mosaic/lib/tests/test_artefacts to remove that copy and restore the device.

details.title: Behavior changes
details.text:
1. Add the smallest regression for the change.
2. Confirm that it fails for the expected reason.
3. Make the production change and rerun the regression.
4. Run affected unit, integration and emulator behavior tests, then the full Lua suite.
Follow AGENTS.md. Documentation does not replace observable acceptance.

title: Masks
summary: Override channel and step trig, note, velocity, length and chord values.
prose:
Masks override attributes of the merged pattern data. They can overwrite pattern values or create steps the patterns do not have, and they accept triggers, notes, velocities and chords. Set a channel default to affect every step, or hold a step to set an individual override. Unset attributes use the channel default or merged pattern data. Each Masks recipe below starts from the four-step loop in Make your first loop (channel 1, pattern 1, steps 1-4). A masked value always wins over the pattern for that step; the channel default wins over the pattern for every step without its own mask.
The Masks screen shows the value you are editing as you turn E3, with note names for the Note row, so stop on the readout instead of counting detents. One detent moves a note by one MIDI note and other values by one unit.

[Masks demo](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=J1ckUZvhFJ0&t=1740s)

details.title: Unset values and precedence
details.text: X is an unset attribute, not zero. A step's explicit attribute wins over the channel default; an unset step uses the default; an unset default falls back to merged pattern data. Clearing step overrides does not erase the defaults.

details.title: Chord masks
details.text: Chd1–Chd4 add four scale-relative voices above or below the root. 3rd and 5th specify intervals, not MIDI note numbers. From X, turn E3 right for a voice above the root and left for a voice below it; each row reaches 14 scale steps either way. Select a polyphonic output to play simultaneous chord voices. Use strum and chord velocity to adjust their timing and level.

details.title: Scale, degree and rotation
details.text: Note masks snap to the selected scale by default. Degree and rotation apply only when full quantisation is enabled. See Snap Note Masks to Scale, Quantise Note Masks and Fully Quantise Mask for their precedence. Turn off Snap note masks to scale in the Mosaic params to enter accidentals or dissonant notes.

details.title: MIDI and clearing
details.text: Hold a step and play a MIDI keyboard to enter notes and chords. Live recording also enters masks. With a step held, K2 clears that step even if K1 is held. Other channels are unaffected.

details.title: If a new note is silent
details.text: Check the selected channel's output, active range and mute state. A trig alone needs an audible note, velocity and length. A mono voice cannot sound all chord voices together. To undo an exception, hold that step and press K2.

details.title: Note names on the Masks screen
details.text: The Masks screen uses norns musicutil: floor(MIDI note / 12 − 2). MIDI note 60 is displayed as C3. The Fixed Note parameter uses a different label convention and displays MIDI note 60 as C5. Use numeric MIDI notes when comparing these controls.

title: Creating a First Loop
summary: Make four equal notes. Start with the sound and tempo from chapter 2. Write four trigs and hear them repeat.
prose:
[Make four equal notes](#first-sound/course) is the complete continuing lesson.

Start here: Start with the sound and tempo from chapter 2. Write four trigs and hear them repeat.

If you are joining with your own project, match that starting state first. Keep the course project open while following the course; the independent examples below use their own stated setup.

details.title: Complete lesson
details.text: Open [Make four equal notes](#first-sound/course) for the ordered actions, their results and the matching listening example. Start with the sound and tempo from chapter 2. Write four trigs and hear them repeat.

details.title: Coordinates and pitches
details.text: The first channel steps run across row 4. Coordinates count from the grid’s top-left corner. Octave labels vary between screens: this tutorial uses the Masks field, where MIDI 60 is C3. Numeric MIDI is the reliable reference when moving between instruments or controls.

details.title: Walkthrough Result
details.text: The walkthrough above shows each setting on screen and plays two cycles of four equal MIDI notes (MIDI 60, velocity 80), then stops playback. It does not include a live audio recording of the first loop.

details.title: Recovery
details.text: If silent, follow [No Sound](#no-sound) in transport → assignment → range → masks → output order.

details.title: Course continuity
details.text: Continue at [Make four equal notes](#first-sound/course). The independent examples have separate starting states; use another project after saving your course piece.

details.title: Independent controls example
details.text:
Before starting: Start a new project with Record off. No output, patterns or masks have been entered yet. The walkthrough below begins by choosing an output for channel 1, so you can follow it from an empty project. [Configuring an Output](#setup) explains the choices.

### Choose the output

1. Tap Channel (3,8). The header reads CH01.
2. Turn E1 to open Channel tasks, select Device with E2 and press K3.
3. Select a working output with E3: the basic MIDI device (CC Device), your own configuration, or Polyperc 1 for internal sound. Press K3 to apply.

Device shows the output you chose. A selection that has not been applied with K3 is only a draft.

### Enter four attacks

1. Tap Pattern (5,8) to Trig. The header names pattern 1.
2. Tap (1,4), (2,4), (3,4), (4,4).

Four active attacks light on row 4. Each lit step is a trig, a point where a note can sound. If you are editing another pattern, select pattern 1 on the top row first.

### Assign and shorten

1. Tap Channel (3,8).
2. Tap pattern slot (1,2).
3. Hold step (1,4), tap (4,4), release (1,4). To set a range, hold its first step, tap its last step, then release the first.

Pattern 1 feeds channel 1 across a four-step range, so the channel loops steps 1 to 4.

### Give the attacks a pitch and level

1. Open Channel tasks → Masks.
2. With no step held, select Note with E2 and set MIDI 60 with E3 (C3). The Masks screen labels MIDI 60 as C3.
3. Select Vel and set 80.
4. Select Len and set 1/2.

These are channel masks: all four attacks share one pitch, velocity and length. A step could override them later.

### Play and stop

1. Tap Play (1,8).
2. Listen for four equal C notes repeating, with a playhead moving along the grid. At 90 BPM and the default Rate /1 each step lasts one sixth of a second, so the loop repeats about every two thirds of a second.
3. Tap Play again to stop; hold K1 too if Shift press stop is enabled.

Four equal C notes repeat. Playback stops with notes released.

Resulting project: Pattern 1 attacks 1–4; CH01 assigned P1; range 1–4; Note 60/Vel 80/Len1/2; no step exceptions; stopped.

title: Troubleshooting No Sound
summary: Check transport, channel data and output settings in order.
prose:
Use the loop in [Creating a First Loop](#first-sound). Check the following in order.

1. Check that the grid playhead moves. If it does not, press Play. For an external clock source, check that the source is running and sending clock. Use the internal clock for a standalone check.
2. Select the intended channel and check that it is unmuted. Assign a pattern or enter trig masks. An unassigned source pattern does not play through the channel.
3. Check that active attacks are inside the channel range. If several patterns are assigned, check whether Skip removes their overlaps. Compare one assigned pattern or All trig merge.
4. Open Masks. Check Trig, Note, Vel and Len at channel and held-step scope. An explicit step value overrides its default. Velocity 0 is silent. Clear an exception to restore inheritance.
5. Open Device. Apply the selection with K3; a draft is not the active destination. For MIDI, match output port and receive channel. For n.b., check that the player is installed, enabled and supported. Check norns audio level and the listening path.

For hanging notes, stop playback, then hold a non-selected page navigation key to invoke panic. Panic sends Note Off messages but does not stop playback. A running sequence can sound new notes after the sweep.

The examples on this page each show one of these checks. Keep each channel independent shows that Device belongs to one channel, so a channel with Device None makes no sound (check 5). Keep a valid range when a gesture is reversed shows the channel range in check 3: a range gesture whose end would come before its start is refused, the previous valid range stays, and only the attacks inside that range sound. Merge two patterns shows how Skip removes the trigs two patterns share (check 3). Set velocity and length masks shows that velocity 0 is silent and that X lets the pattern's own velocity through (check 4). Create a four-step loop from an empty project is the working loop to compare against.

title: Creating a Phrase and Arrangement

details.title: Restore Pattern Note Inheritance
details.text:
The first loop leaves CH01 Note C3 (MIDI 60), Vel 80 and Len 1/2 channel masks. These still override matching pattern values. Before editing relative pattern notes, stop playback. Tap Channel (3,8), turn E1 to Channel tasks, select Masks with E2 and press K3. With no step held, select Note with E2 and turn E3 until the field reads X. X is unset, not zero; on steps without a step-specific note mask, the merged pattern note now plays. Keep Vel and Len at 80 and 1/2, or set them to X if pattern values should control them too.
K1+K2 with no step held clears channel step overrides but preserves defaults; it does not clear Note C3. To clear all masks on one step, hold that step and press K2. See Masks: Unset values and precedence.

details.title: Independent controls example
details.text:
Before starting: Use channel 1 with pattern 1 assigned, active attacks at steps 1–4 and range 1–4. Set channel Masks Note to MIDI 60, Vel to 80 and Len to 1/2; clear existing step exceptions. Stop playback. [Creating a First Loop](#first-sound) gives the complete preparation route.

### Extend the range

1. Tap Channel (3,8).
2. Hold (1,4), tap (16,4), release.
3. Turn E1 to Channel tasks; select Clock with E2 and press K3.
4. Select Rate with E2; set /1 with E3 (sixteenth notes, the default).
5. Press K3 to apply while stopped.

The channel traverses16 steps before repeating.

### Move the attacks

1. Open Pattern Trig, pattern 1.
2. Remove steps 2,3,4.
3. Add steps 5,9,13; keep step 1.

Four attacks now sit on the four beats. The old attacks have been removed explicitly.

### Hear the longer phrase

1. Play two bars.
2. Stop.

C–C–C–C remains the pitch sequence; the space between attacks has increased.

Resulting project: P1 attacks 1/5/9/13; CH01 range 1–16; sixteenth-note rate; Note 60/Vel 80/Len1/2 unchanged.

The examples below extend this phrase. Set channel and step note masks shows how a step's own note beats the channel default. Save D major, then apply it shows how a scale slot can be edited and saved without changing what plays until you apply it. The last three examples walk through the whole workflow in order: Add a second pattern in D major merges two patterns on channel 1, Add a second channel with its own output gives channel 2 its own MIDI port, and Chain song slots an octave apart plays two song slots.

details.text:
Before starting: Use any stopped project containing a named arrangement. The worked reload check uses slot 1 with channel 1 muted and another channel audible. For another project, make a reversible visible change before loading and confirm the saved state returns.

### Save the arrangement

1. Tap K1 briefly to enter the norns system menu.
2. Open PARAMS → MOSAIC → Save project.
3. Press K3 to open text entry. Turn E2 left to DEL and press K3 three times to remove new. Turn E3 left to the character row; use E2 to select each character of Four notes and K3 to enter it, including the space. Turn E3 right to the bottom row, turn E2 right to OK, and press and release K3. K2 cancels text entry.

The named project stores the two-section arrangement.

### Prove the saved version

1. Return to Mosaic, select Song slot 1, then open Channel.
2. Hold K1, tap channel 1 at (1,1), release K1 to unmute it temporarily.
3. With playback stopped, open PARAMS → MOSAIC → Load project.
4. Select Four notes and confirm.

Slot 1 returns to bass alone; the temporary change is removed.

### Replay the restored sections

1. Select slot 1.
2. Play four section passes and stop.

The saved bass-only/full-phrase alternation is restored. Continue with merge, recording or modulation task guides without replacing this saved version.

Resulting project: Named project Four notes contains both sections and restores their exact playback. Transport stopped with no held notes.

title: Four-Bar Percussion, Bass and Chord Example
summary: Build a four-bar loop of drums, bass and a moving chord on three channels at 90 BPM in C major.
prose:
Build a four-bar loop on three channels: Oilcan 1 plays drums on channel 1, Polyperc 1 plays a bass line on channel 2 and Doubledecker plays chords on channel 3. The drum and bass phrases repeat unchanged in every bar. Only the chord roots change, in bar 4, so you hear the harmony move while the groove stays put. Play "Rhythm, bass and a changing chord" under Listen to hear the finished result first.

Before you start:

1. Set 90 BPM in Song tasks → Tempo & feel (E3, then K3). Keep the default Rate /1 on every channel: one step is a sixteenth note, 16 steps are one bar and 64 steps are four bars.

2. Set the range of channels 1–3 to steps 1–64.

3. Open PARAMS > MOSAIC and set Snap note masks to scale to Off, so that MIDI 37 (C#1) in the drum channel is not snapped to C major.

How notes are entered in these recipes: open Masks (grid (3,8), E1 to tasks, E2 to Masks, K3). E2 chooses the value (Trig, Note, Vel, Len, Chd1–Chd4). With no step held, E3 sets the channel default, which every step uses unless it has its own value. Hold K1 and tap a step to add or remove a trig on it. Hold a step and turn E3 to give that step its own value. Hold a step and press K2 to remove its own values. The grid shows sixteen steps at a time: bar 1 is steps 1–16, bar 2 is steps 17–32, bar 3 is steps 33–48 and bar 4 is steps 49–64, so move to the right sixteen-step page before you tap steps in a later bar. In bars after the first, add 16 to each step number of bar 1.

Build the channels in order: Percussion Channel, Bass Channel, Chord Channel. Press Play after each one to hear the loop grow before you add the next channel.

Finish with a contrasting section: open the Song Editor, copy the song slot and mute one channel in the copy (see Song Composition). Numeric MIDI notes are used throughout, because Masks shows MIDI 36, 48 and 60 as C1, C2 and C3 while other controls label octaves differently. Each n.b. player is unique: Polyperc 1 cannot be assigned to another channel once it is assigned to the bass.

details.title: Recorded Example: Rhythm, bass and a changing chord
details.text:
Four bars at 90 BPM.

Channel 1, Oilcan 1, velocity 38: in every bar MIDI 36 on steps 1 and 9, MIDI 38 on steps 4 and 12 and MIDI 37 on steps 5 and 13.

Channel 2, Polyperc 1, velocity 42: in every bar MIDI 48 on steps 1, 5 and 13 and MIDI 55 on step 9.

Channel 3, Doubledecker, velocity 26, three steps long, Chd1 3rd and Chd2 5th: in bars 1 to 3 the chord roots are MIDI 60 on step 1 and MIDI 62 on step 9 of the bar. In bar 4 they are MIDI 67 on step 49 and MIDI 60 on step 57.

Play the loop and listen for the chord at the start of bar 4: the drums and bass are unchanged, while the chords move from C and D to G and C.

title: Adding a Ghost Note
summary: Compare two bars of main hits with two bars that add a quiet hit before an accent.
prose:
Compare two ways of playing the same four-beat drum figure on Oilcan 1. Bars 1 and 2 contain only the main hits (MIDI 36 on steps 1 and 9, MIDI 37 on steps 5 and 13, all at velocity 90). Bars 3 and 4 add one quiet hit, MIDI 38 at velocity 35, on step 12 of the bar, just before the accent on step 13. This is a ghost note: a soft hit that adds movement without changing the main hits.

Settings: 90 BPM, Rate /1 (the default, one step is a sixteenth note), range 1–64 and length ½ step on all notes. Play "Adding a Ghost Note" under Listen to hear the target, then build it with the first recipe.

Two further recipes follow: an optional probability variation of the ghost notes, and a separate, denser drum pattern at velocity 48 (the "Three sounds, one pocket" recording) that does not use ghost notes.

title: Changing Harmony with Scale Slots
summary: Compare the same relative patterns under C major for two bars and D major for two bars.
prose:
Hear one pair of relative-note patterns in two keys. Doubledecker on channel 1 plays an upper phrase and Polyperc 1 on channel 2 plays a bass. For bars 1 and 2 the global scale is C major (scale slot 1); for bars 3 and 4 it is D major (scale slot 2). The patterns hold scale degrees, not fixed pitches, and the Note masks stay X (unset), so changing the applied scale moves every pitch while rhythm, velocity and length stay the same. Play "Changing Harmony with Scale Slots" under Listen to hear the target.

Settings: 90 BPM, Rate /1 (the default, one step is a sixteenth note) and a 16-step range that loops once per bar. The bass velocity is 60 and its notes last ½ step in this comparison. The "A bass with room above it" recording is a different example, in fixed notes in C major.

title: Combining Four-Step and Three-Step Loops
summary: Use independent channel lengths to create a 12-step repeating relationship.
prose:
Run two channels at the same clock rate with different lengths: channel 1 loops a four-step phrase and channel 2 loops a three-step phrase. Both channels start together on step 1, drift apart, and meet again after 12 steps, the smallest number that both 4 and 3 divide into. At the default Rate /1 and 90 BPM, 12 steps last two seconds. Playback is continuous: each channel simply starts its own loop again when it reaches the end of its range.

1. On channel 1, assign a pattern with active steps 1–4. Using the default C-major scale, set relative pattern notes 0, 1, 2 and 3, which produce MIDI 60, 62, 64 and 65. Set the velocities to 127, 117, 107 and 97 and each note length to one step. Set the range to steps 1–4 (hold step 1, tap step 4, release step 1).

2. On channel 2, assign the same pattern and set the range to steps 1–3.

3. Open channel 2 Masks. With no step held, set the channel defaults to Note MIDI 79, Vel 40 and Len ½.

4. Hold step 2 and set Note MIDI 81, Vel 60 and Len 1¼. Release the step. Channel 2 now repeats MIDI 79, 81, 79, independent of the four notes on channel 1.

5. Start playback. Both channels begin together. Compare their first steps again after 12 steps (about two seconds).

6. Stop playback before changing the arrangement.

Use separate MIDI routes for the two instruments. For internal sound, assign different supported players, for example Polyperc 1 for channel 1 and Doubledecker for channel 2. Song transitions and reset options can restart channels earlier than 12 steps; the second recipe shows how.
